Finally, the detection results are used for the estimation of ship heading and speed. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has high detection accuracy for linear wake features in complex background.

articleTitle: High-Performance Unequal Power Splitter Based on Ferrite Cores
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design procedure of unequal power splitters with arbitrary integer power ratio based on ferrite cores. The unequal power splitter is developed from the transformer-type Wilkinson power splitters. As an example, a 2:1 power splitter operated in 3~300 MHz is proposed, where lumped components are carefully selected to match the input and output ports. The measurement results demonstrate that the VSWR of the input and output ports are less than 1.2, the isolation between the two output ports is more than 27 dB and the insertion loss is less than 0.6 dB. Such power splitters have small dimensions and very low cost.

articleTitle: Five-order Equal Ripple Wideband Bandpass Filter with Minimized Variation in Group Delay
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband bandpass filter, consisting of two shunt short-circuited stubs and a two-staged cascading coupled line section, is presented. The analytical study reveals that an equal-ripple response in magnitude and the flattest group delay can be achieved simultaneously in passband when choosing the impedances of the lines properly. In addition, those impedances can be determined exactly by solving a set of equations describing the matching between the transfer function of the filter topology and a target function with equal-ripple response. For verification, two filter samples with different design specifications are designed, simulated and discussed.

articleTitle: Multiple Random Phase-Screen Simulation of Scintillation Effect of Bessel-Gaussian Beam in Ocean Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the generalized huygens-fresnel principle, this paper use the power spectrum inversion method to produce ocean turbulent phase screen simulation model. And study the Bessel-Gaussian beam(BGB) scintillation characteristics in ocean turbulence. The results show that the higher the turbulence of the ocean is, the more serious the phase distortion is, the more obvious the scintillation is, and gradually degenerates into the normal Gaussian beam(GB). With the increase of transmission distance, the increase of the order of the BGB, the increase of waveform parameters, and the decrease of the rate of dissipation of kinetic energy per unit mass of water are the stronger the scintillation effect in the ocean turbulence. And the BGB has a critical beam width value, which is far away from the value and its scintillation effect is stronger in ocean turbulence. The study provides a theoretical basis for the transmission and communication of vortex beam in ocean turbulence.

articleTitle: A Helix Antenna with Broad Beamwidth for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a microstrip fed helix antenna with more than 40% bandwidth is presented. The application of conventional helix antenna was limited by radiation pattern in different fields. By this means, a novel rhomboid plate structure is employed to widened beamwidth of the helix antenna in the whole bands. The beamwidth of the proposed antenna is reduced to ± 60° over the impedance matching bandwidth ranging from 8GHz to 12GHz , which is an improvement to the previously reported helix antennas.

articleTitle: The Far-field Estimation for Microstrip Line Based on Near-field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Far-field test of device is a very significant way for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) diagnose. And the far-field emission estimation typically requires the accurate information of noise source which usually may not be feasible. Microstrip line is one of the main radiation sources of printed circuit board (PCB), and the surface current on which causes the far-field emission. An efficient numerical equivalent source model based on near-field scanning is proposed in this paper. The near-field tangential component of magnetic field is measured by a magnetic probe to obtain an equivalent source. And the far-field estimation is calculated by this numerical source model. It will save a lot of time compared with the fullwave simulation and far-field test in anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: High power microwave system based on power combination and pulse compression of conventional klystrons
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high power microwave system based on power combination and pulse compression of conventional klystrons is introduced in this paper. This system mainly consists of pulse modulator, power combiner, driving source of klystrons and pulse compressor. A solid state induction modulator and pulse transformer were used to drive two 50MW S-band klystrons with pulse widths 4μs in parallel, after power combination and pulse compression, the tested peak power had reached about 210MW with pulse widths nearly 400 ns at 25Hz, while the experimental maximum output power was just limited by the power capacity of loads. This type of high power microwave system has widely application prospects in RF system of large scale particle accelerators, high power radar transmitters and high level electromagnetic environment generators.

articleTitle: Design of Structural-reliable X-band High-gain Vivaldi Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a structural reliable high-gain Vivaldi array antenna over 8-12 GHz for airborne reconnaissance and surveillance operations. The overall size of the array is 190mm×200mm×170mm. The measured minimum gain is 20.5 dBi and the measured VSWR is less than 1.8 over the entire X-band. In the harsh operating environment, the specific shape aluminum plate can ensure the antenna work for long hours.

articleTitle: Calibration measurement of shore-based radar with active reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radar external calibration is an important means to obtain the radar cross section (RCS) of unknown target. The choice of calibration method is closely related to the ambient environment of the radar station. This paper reports a calibration measurement of the UHF-band shore-based radar with active radar calibrator (ARC) on a fishing boat. It was found that multipath propagation effect due to the sea surface could not be eliminated as due to the ground. Based on the analysis of multi-path model, our experiment solved the problem of multi-path propagation better, and the calibration precision is controlled at 2dB.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of the Interaction Between Electromagnetic Waves and Ionosphere During Parametric Decay Instability (PDI) Process
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, based on the two-fluid magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) theory, the advanced finite-difference time-domain method have been conducted to successfully simulate the variability in the electric field, magnetic field and plasma number density during the parametric decay instability (PDI) process driven by electromagnetic (EM) waves. As a result, the mode-conversion process of Langmuir waves excited by ordinary mode EM waves was visualized at the turning point at the millisecond timescale, which is an important characteristic of the PDI process. It was found that the ionospheric electron number density rapidly oscillates with the high-frequency (HF) Langmuir waves. Ionospheric ion density depletion was also observed at the cutoff altitude and two ion density peaks were simultaneously observed on both sides of the EM wave reflection region. These results are of benefit to understand the nonlinear interaction between EM waves and the ionosphere.

articleTitle: Spatial Polarization Characteristics of Wide-angle Scanning Slot Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Antenna polarization states always varied with scan direction, a new concept of spatial polarization characteristics of antenna is defined in this thesis. Phased-array behaves distinct property compared to mechanically-scanned antenna. The wave-guide slot phased array is used in this paper to study the polarization property with wide angle scan in airspace. Theoretical analysis and simulation proved that the lobe property and polarization changes not much in the case of small azimuth and elevation scanning angle. However, there is dramatic increase of cross polarization component in the main lobe with wide scanning angle. This characteristic can be applied to measure the target polarization scattering property in phased array radar searching stage. Based on the single polarized radar antenna, a novel polarization scattering matrix (PSM) measurement method is proposed by sufficiently utilizing the inherent polarization property of antenna which is not constant but a function of antenna's spatial scanning direction. Two orthogonal polarization channels are not required in this method. Just by using the prior knowledge of antenna polarization characteristics and improving the signal processing mode of received radar signal, the PSM of target can be obtained.

articleTitle: Design of an X-band Antenna on Airborne Craft with Omnidirection Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An octagonal prism conformal antenna array for x-band with vertically polarized omnidirectional radiation pattern is presented in this letter. The proposed antenna consists of a feeding network, radiation patches, parasitic patches, and dielectric layer. The 16 patches are placed on the outer surface of the octagonal cylinder and fed by a feeding network with uniform magnitude and phase. The patches are divided into upper and lower layers, each of which has eight units. Thus, the proposed antenna can obtain an omnidirectional radiation. To enhance the isolation between the elements, slots are introduced to decrease electromagnetic coupling between elements through the medium. By utilizing 16 conformal patches, the gain in the horizontal plane can be improved, especially for the range of θ=80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to θ=100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. The proposed antenna is designed and simulated. Simulation results reveal that the proposed antenna can provide an impedance bandwidth of 20% (7.16-8.76 GHz). Additionally, the minimum gain of the range which from θ=80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to θ=100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> is greater than 2.8 dBi over the frequency band.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging Method for Non-Cooperative Slow Rotation Targets in Space
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Considering the electromagnetic scattering and ISAR echo of space non-cooperative targets with slow rotation characteristics, in this paper, combined with the motion characteristics of target rigid body, a spatial non-cooperative security ISAR imaging method based on SRMF and CLEAN algorithm is proposed. According to the motion feature of the target and the related parameters, firstly the model of the target geometry and the scattering echo is established, and then the echo signal is translational compensation and the slow angular velocity is estimated. Finally, a two-dimensional ISAR image of the target is achieved by estimating the angular velocity. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and practicability of the method.

articleTitle: Kinetic modeling of stimulated electromagnetic emissions during ionospheric heating experiment
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Stimulated electromagnetic emissions (SEEs) induced by high power electromagnetic waves injected into ionospheric plasmas provide direct parameter retrieval and assessment of nonlinear wave-particle interaction in the resonance regime. The broad upshifted maximum (BUM) is the most prominent spectral line in ionospheric stimulated electromagnetic radiation, which is associated with artificial ionization layers. A parametric process responsible for the generation of the BUM is investigated by two-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell simulations. Preliminary results show that simulated frequency spectra of the BUM emission agrees with experimental observations near the fourth electron gyroharmonic 4fce. Towards developing reliable SEE sensing techniques, this model provides a powerful tool for investigating stimulated electromagnetic emissions and associated plasma parameters.

articleTitle: Experimental study on surface scattering characteristics of wall and ground in the millimeter wave
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the millimeter wave, especially the high-end three-dimensional communication of the millimeter wave, the influence of the millimeter wave scattering on the rough ground surface and the wall surface makes it impossible to adopt the specular reflection only. Based on the test data of the wall and ground surfaces at different incident angles at 28 GHz, the distribution of the scattering signals of the millimeter wave at different incident angles is obtained, then the scattering characteristics of the wall and the ground surfaces are analyzed. The results show that there is not only a diffuse scattering phenomenon near the direction of the specular reflection on both the wall and the ground surfaces, but also in other directions. So it is especially important to introduce diffuse scattering in the ray tracing method.

articleTitle: Linear-to-circular Polarization Converter Utilizing Double-arc-based Metasurface at Terahertz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Polarization is a property of electromagnetic waves and plays an irreplaceable role in electromagnetic devices. In this paper, we propose a reflective polarization converter in terahertz regime, which utilizes the double-arc-based metasurface and can efficiently convert the linear polarized wave into the circular polarized wave. The polarization converter achieves an excellent effect that the reflection coefficient amplitude of the two reflection components is approximately equal to 0.7 in the frequency range of 0.59-1.38THz, while the phase difference between the two components is about 90° or -270°. Meanwhile, the ellipticity of proposed polarization converter is close to 1 in the operating frequency band with the conversion efficiency ≥ 80%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ultra-short Wave Propagation in Atmospheric Duct
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the phenomenon of Ship-borne AIS over-the-horizon communication in some area in the Yellow Sea in June 2, 2018, which influenced by atmospheric duct, the atmospheric duct is calculated by using the atmospheric temperature and humidity profiles measured at that time. According to the calculated atmospheric duct environment, the parabolic numerical equation model and the AIS coverage evaluation model are used to analyze the maximum distance of AIS in the atmospheric duct environment. The results show that this method can be used to evaluate the maximum range of AIS and other ultra-short wave equipment under complex refraction environment conditions such as atmospheric duct. Meanwhile, it also shows that the characteristics of atmospheric duct can be inferred based on over-the-horizon communication distance of AIS.

articleTitle: Low Profile SIW Cavity-Backed Magneto-Electric Dipole with Wide Beamwidth Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the complementary antenna concept of combining an electric dipole with a magnetic dipole, a linearly polarized substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) cavity-backed magneto-electric(ME) dipole antenna has been proposed. This antenna has wide beamwidth radiation patterns. The half-power beamwidths (HPBW) are 175° in E-plane and 130° in H-plane. Besides, the proposed antenna has a low profile of about 0.03 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the space wavelength at center operating frequency) with good radiation performances across the impedance bandwidth including a stable gain, symmetrically unidirectional radiation patterns in both of the two principal planes and especially, a significantly low cross polarization. The antenna is designed, fabricated and measured. Measured results show a good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Scattering verification and imaging of vegetation and its components
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The scattering of a 3-D deterministic forest scene is calculated for simulating the synthetic aperture radar(SAR) image. The generated trees are simplified as a cluster of slim cylinders and disks with the deterministic location, orientation and dielectric constant, which are used for coherent scattering calculation. To ensure the accuracy of coherent scattering calculation, the validity of the generalized Rayleigh-Gans (GRG) approximation and the infinite cylinder approximation are verified. The scattering of tree's components is verified by comparing the imaging results of the calculated data and the simulated data.

articleTitle: 220GHz High Gain On-chip Antenna Based on 180nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip integrated antenna based on 180nm-CMOS process. By loading the artificial magnetic conductor(AMC) structure under the antenna, the antenna gain is improved and the radiation pattern is optimized. The peak gain of this antenna reaches 9.6 dBi with low side lobes. The bandwidth is increased to 212-227GHz by using a special structural connection between the feed line and the antenna.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Massive MIMO System in Indoor Scenario
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is a potential candidate key technology for the fifth generation of wireless communication systems. In research to date, many investigations are based on theoretical channels with independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh channels. In this paper, we focus on how a massive MIMO system performs in real propagation environments, specifically on channel performance of a realistic indoor scenario using large linear and circular antenna arrays. With massive MIMO, as the number of antennas increases and becomes much larger than the number of users, we get smaller singular value spreads and better orthogonality between user channels, what's more, the singular value spreads become more stable over channel realizations. The stability of singular value spread implies that bad channel conditions can be largely avoided. By analyzing the singular value spread of a massive MIMO system, it shows the measured channel can achieve performance close to the i.i.d. Rayleigh channel. So it can be conclude that the theoretical advantages of massive MIMO can also be harvest in real channel.

articleTitle: Test of an ionospheric activity index using foF2 data in China
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An index to describe the storm time ionospheric variation is derived from the historical data in China. This index is tested using data for different seasons and stations of China. The result indicates that this index is suitable for representing the variation of ionospheric activity during storm time in China.

articleTitle: A method for grading evaluation of the atmospheric refraction effect on the radio marginalline-of-sight distance
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Different atmospheric refraction conditions could affect the radio marginal line-of-sight (LoS) distance and the scope of operation of radio system significantly. For vast number of radio system users to understand and use the standards of radio marginal LoS distance more intuitively, this paper presents a grading evaluation method based on the radio line-of-sight index as characterization factor, according to the degree and probability of radio marginal LoS distance deviating from the standard line-of-sight. On the basis of this, the possible influence of the radio line-of-sight index of different levels on the radio system is analyzed, as well as the influence of atmospheric refraction on the radio line-of-sight is described intuitively. This paper gives the distribution of the percentage of time of near ground the radio line-of-sight index in China.

articleTitle: A Two-dimensional Low Side Lobe Frequency Scanning Planar Array with Hybrid Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A 1×4 two-dimensional low side lobe frequency scanning planar array with hybrid feeding structure in Ku-band has been designed. In order to obtain low side lobe, the planar array was designed by 4 parallel sub-arrays in azimuth dimension and the electromagnetically coupled feeding structure was used to ensure non-uniform distribution of energy. The results of simulation show that, except at the center frequency, the voltage standing wave ratio(VSWR) of the antenna array is below 1.2 at the operation band, the range of the scanning angles is (-30.5°, 29°), the beam width of the antenna is about 5.5-6.6 degrees, and the gain is more than 30dBi. The measure results of side lobe in azimuth dimension are below -19dB, and the results of side lobe in pitch dimension are below -25dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Shared Aperture Dual-Band Slot Array
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper designed a novel shared aperture dual-band slot array. The array is a planar mono pulse antenna. The Ku band slot array is interlaced to the C band slot array to make the dual-band antenna radiate in the same plane. The Ku band slot array is fed by waveguide, and the C band slot array is fed by strip line, which not only ensures high antenna efficiency but also reduces the weight and size of the antenna. Antenna simulation and prototype measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Simulation of Indoor MIMO Channel Propagation Characteristics Based on the SBR Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 4×4 indoor MIMO (Multiple-Input and Multiple-Output) system is simulated based on the SBR (Shooting and Bouncing Ray) method. In order to estimate the performance of MIMO system, the impacts of antenna polarization and signal frequency on propagation characteristics such as path loss, capacity, throughput are studied in both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight link.

articleTitle: A Framework of Integrated Service System of Ionospheric Scintillation Information
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The researchers, system designers and equipment operators may need related information of ionospheric scintillations for special wireless applications. A framework of integrated service system of ionospheric scintillation information is put forward, which could provide information services of the effects of ionospheric irregularities on trans-ionospheric radio signals to support related operations.

articleTitle: The Design of A 3–18GHz Tightly Coupled Dipole Array with An FSS Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a design for ultra-wideband tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) with a Marchand balun and a printed frequency selective surface (FSS) for wide angle scanning. The simulation results show that the infinite array achieves 6:1 bandwidth (3-18GHz) with VSWR<;2.5 in the broadside while scanning up to ±45° in the E and H planes for VSWR<;3, <; -20dB cross-polarization. The FSS superstrate replaces the bulky dielectric layer, leading to a low profile and low weight structure. In comparison to strip feed line, the tapered micro-strip feed line makes the model easier to fabricate at high frequency.

articleTitle: Computation of Bessel Beams in the FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the angular spectrum representation (ASR) of the Bessel beams, Bessel beam sources are generated in three-dimensional FDTD using the total-field/scattered-field (TF/ST) method. The correctness and accuracy of the method are verified by comparing the reconstructed field in FDTD with the original field. Comparisons of scattering intensity diagrams calculated using FDTD and those obtained using the generalized Lorenz-Mie theory (GLMT) are implemented for a dielectric sphere illuminated by a Bessel beam, very good agreements have been achieved. The approach presented in this paper can be applied to generate other structured beam sources in FDTD, which provides an access to solve structured beam scattering by complex particles using FDTD.

articleTitle: Doppler Spectrum of Backscattered Field from Time-Varying Sea with a Low-Flying Small Target Above It
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the Doppler spectrum of backscattered echoes from moving target above time-varying sea surfaces is investigated by utilizing the quasi-stationary algorithm, i.e., approximating the time-domain problem by repeatedly implementing the frequency-domain method. In order to fast and accurately solve the composite scattering problem of time-varying sea surfaces with a Low-flying small target above it, a hybrid algorithm of Kirchhoff approximation (KA) and method method-of-moments (MoM) is utilized in this paper for analyzing the Doppler spectrum signatures. The effect of the speed of flying target on Doppler spectrum signatures of a low-flying small target above time-varying sea surface is investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Observations of Traveling Ionospheric Disturbances in the mid-latitudes using combined Ionosphere sounding
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An experiment system for the ionosphere combined sounding is established based on the Stations-Net of the National Radio Environment Monitor. The system, which monitors the ionosphere for the presence of traveling ionospheric disturbances (T.I.D.s.), includes various instruments of ionosphere detection, such as backscatter sounding, vertical sounding, and oblique sounding. The characteristics of T.I.D.s. in the vertical, oblique, and backscatter propagation with radio in the ionosphere are described using the model and ray trace method. Through an analysis of the experiment system of sweep and fixed frequency sounding data in the coverage of both distance (500 km to over 2500 km) and azimuth (60°), the technical feasibility of distinguishing the presence of T.I.D.s. is explored. And the parameters of T.I.D.s. are also obtained. The monitoring capability of the experiment system for T.I.D.s. is demonstrated through long term experimental data at mid-latitudes, which is the mesh of monitoring areas of backscatter sounding and the ionosphere combined sounding with multi-monitoring means.

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis of the effects of magnetic declination on flux-tube integrated linear growth rate of generalized Rayleigh-Taylor instability
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The influence of different longitude and magnetic deflection on the neutral wind are studied, using the method of flux-tube integration. The results indicate that magnetic deflection on the integral neutral wind perpendicular to the magnetic meridian has less influence, but the influence of magnetic deflection on the integral neutral wind perpendicular to the magnetic field line in the meridian is significant. What's more, the influence of magnetic declination on integral neutral wind is evidently dependent on longitude. The neutral wind and magnetic declination in the ionosphere are the main factors leading to the north-south asymmetry of electron density and its gradient, which may affect the generation and evolution of irregular structure and Rayleigh-Taylor instability, and the variation of irregular structure with season and solar activity as well as the distribution of geographic longitude and latitude. This is a question worthy of further study.

articleTitle: The Improved Optic Design of CFETR ECRH Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) is the key auxiliary heating system in Chinese Fusion Engineering Test Reactor (CFETR). The function of ECRH antenna is to inject the high and long-pulse RF power into plasma for heating, current driving and other physics applications. The optical transmission characteristic of gaussian beams decides the ability of antenna. Two improved optic designs based on the previous analysis of the initial small size CFETR are provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Distribution Prediction of SLF/ELF Atmospheric Radio Noise in China
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to identify the abnormity of the SLF (Super Low Frequency)/ELF (Extremely Low Frequency) electromagnetic radiation before the earthquake, it needs to study the distribution of the spatial SLF/ELF atmospheric radio noise in China. The atmospheric radio noise is substantially the total contribution of the radiation fields excited by the lightning. The main frequency spectrum of the lightning electric current is from VLF (Very Low Frequency) to SLF. The variations of the atmospheric radio noise envelope level root-mean-square value with the frequency can be obtained for the different time periods in the different seasons by analyzing the published data and AD report. It can be obtained the variations of 80Hz atmospheric radio noise envelope level root-mean-square value along the time and the months for the different time periods in the different seasons at Qingdao, Kunming and Huhehaote in China.

articleTitle: Investigation of Miniaturized Wideband Circular-polarized Cavity-Backed Printed Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new crossed printed dipole antenna is proposed for the circular polarization, and the cavity technique is used to realize directional radiation and enhance the gain. The radiator consists of two vertical non-uniform butterfly-shaped dipoles, which are printed on the substrate of FR-4, and as well two parasitic strips vertical to the short dipole are added at the same layer to broaden the AR bandwidth. The dipoles are fed by the Balun where the contiguous monopoles of the two different dipoles are one pair as one of two feeding points. Moreover, the cavity is filled with the dielectric of FR-4 to greatly miniaturize the cavity dimension. Then the final overall size of the proposed antenna is 10mm*35mm*35mm (0.154λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>*0.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>*0.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the lowest working frequency.

articleTitle: Characteristics of GPS Ionospheric Scintillations over Sanya and Guilin
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The characteristics of Chinese low-latitude ionospheric scintillations were investigated by using two GPS receivers installed at Sanya (18.3°N, 109.6°E; geomagnetic: 8.39°N, 181.97°E) and Guilin (25.29°N, 110.33°E; geomagnetic: 15.35°N, 182.62°E), respectively. The results are presented for data collected during the period from January 2012 to December 2014, which includes the peak of the solar cycle 24 that occurred in 2014. The results show that scintillations over Sanya and Guilin occurred mostly during local night, and scintillations took place mainly during the equinox months. Scintillations over Sanya occurred more frequently than that over Guilin. However, the scintillation intensity over Guilin was stronger than that over Sanya. For both Guilin and Sanya, the annual occurrence rate of scintillations increased with the increased solar activities. Moreover, the occurrence of scintillations over Guilin had obvious equinoctial asymmetry, namely, scintillations occurred more frequently during the vernal equinox months than during the autumn equinox months. Furthermore, the causes of the GPS scintillations features observed over Sanya and Guilin were discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Low Conversion Loss Mixers Design Using Reflector Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents development of low conversion loss fundamental mixers. Appropriate reflector networks are employed to provide proper terminations for operation frequencies and other undesired frequency mixing components in the designed Ka-band single-ended mixer and X-band single balanced mixer. Quantitative analysis of the mixer terminations is presented. Syntheses of the input and output reflector networks are optimized for the mixers. The measured conversion loss of the X-band mixer is 6.4±0.7dB from 10 to 11.5GHz, the lowest conversion loss is 5.67dB at 10.6GHz. RF-IF port isolation is better than 27dB, LO-IF port isolation is higher than 24dB and LO-RF port isolation is better than 14dB. To the Ka-band mixer, the lowest measured conversion loss is 3.52dB at 32.2GHz, the conversion loss is flat and less than 5.68dB from 29 to 34GHz.

articleTitle: A new TMA method for state estimation of underwater target
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel target motion analysis (TMA) method using unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) based on modified polar coordinates (MPC) is proposed to improve the localization accuracy for underwater target with constant velocity. The proposed approach utilizes bearings of two-arrays to estimate the localization and velocity of the target. Unlike extended Kalman filter, unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), which is biased and sensitive to the initial value in Cartesian coordinate, the proposed scheme is much more stable and asymptotically unbiased. Moreover, the performances among these schemes are compared based on the noisy bearings from towed array sonar and flank array sonar via Monte Carlo simulations. Simulation results show that the proposed MPC-UKF has better performances with higher numerical stability and little cost of computational complexity.

articleTitle: On the Virtual Cell Power Allocation in Ultra Dense Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ultra-dense network (UDN) can meet ultra-high peak rate, traffic density and density by densely deploying low-power base stations (BSs). The traditional iterative search water filling (ISWF) algorithm requires many iterations to obtain the optimal power allocation. We adopt a low-complexity iterative water filling (LAWF) algorithm to reduce iterations. We propose sorting water filling (SWF) algorithm. The simulation results show that the sum rate achieved by the LAWF and SWF are better than ISWF. With deployment of UDN, speed and presentation of SWFs are increasing.

articleTitle: Adjustment and Testing of an S-Ku Bands Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 8×8 S-Ku bands tightly coupled dipole array(TCDA) is realized. It is based on the 3-18GHz periodic unit which was proposed by Markus H. Novak et al. The layout of periodic unit is retained with parameters are adjusted. Microstrip power divider, structural fasterner and SMP coaxial connector were added to the simulation model of periodic unit. The active VSWR of periodic unit was less than 2.5 from 2.9GHz to 19.4GHz. The test results of its 8×8 scale array show that the active VSWR of each array element is less than 2.8 from 4.5GHz to 18GHz and less than 4.3 from 3GHz to 4.5GHz. The array radiation efficiency is greater than 70% from 3GHz to 5GHz, greater than 85% from 5GHz to15GHz, and greater than 70% from 15GHz to 18GHz.

articleTitle: A Design of 9kHz-0.5GHz Low Noise Amplifier with High Gain and Smooth Flatness
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wide band (UWB) low noise amplifier (LNA) of bandwidth 9 kHz-0.5 GHz, gain more than 30 dB, flatness fluctuating in ±0.8 dB, noise-figure less than 3 dB and the input and output reflection coefficient is less than -12dB within the range of the bandwidth is designed and measured. This LNA utilizes parallel negative-feedback between the base electrode and the collector electrode with an inductance in series with a resistance to compensate the decrease of the high frequency gain. In addition, an inductance in series with capacitance (LC) circuit is used as the signal coupling path at the input of the amplifier and a π-type attenuation network is used at the output port to improve the return loss respectively at the input and output ends of the amplifier. Compared with the traditional negative feedback amplifier circuit, the above improvement measures can improve gain-flatness and expand bandwidth obviously. Furthermore, this design adopt two stage cascade technology to achieve high gain and low noise figure. Simulation and measurement results are in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Discrete Dipole Approximation for Predicting Far-Field Pattern of Slotted Waveguide Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, We present a numerical technique for predicting the far-field pattern of slotted waveguide antennas based on an adaptation form of the discrete dipole approximation (DDA). By using this method, we can predict the radiation pattern of slotted waveguide antennas with different congurations. The capabilities of the proposed method are verified by demonstrating the excellent agreement between DDA and full-wave solver HFSS. The proposed method has potential application value in the feilds of beamforming and microwave imaging.

articleTitle: On the Propagation of the High-altitude Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A second-order integral equation method (IEM) was introduced to simulate the high-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) in our former report. Here the second-order IEM is used to analyze the propagation characteristics of the HEMP. The near field part and far field part of the HEMP are calculated separately to see which takes more important roles in the radiation of the HEMP. A simplified IEM is also introduced during this process, and computing time and memory are saved. The results show that the transverse electromagnetic field consists mainly of far field, and the radial electric field is generated only by the nearby current source.

articleTitle: Keynote Speeches
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the keynote presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Sideflash striking on the side wall of tall buildings
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Sideflash is a kind of lightning striking on the side wall of tall buildings. This unexpected thunder stroke often leads to big property losses and endangers lives of people. However, the origin and development mechanism of this lightning stroke are still not clear. To simulate the sideflash, a 3-D numerical model of negative cloud-to-ground lightning is built which is composed of two parts: the thundercloud model and the stepped leader model. The thundercloud model is based on the 3-D dynamics and electrification coupled model. And the stepped leader model is based on the Dielectric Breakdown Model (DBM). The Poisson's Equation solved by the Successive Over-Relaxation method is employed to refresh the spatial electric potential field. Finally, some buildings with different heights are set on the ground. In the numerical simulation, some sideflashes are observed. Based on the comparison experiments, the origin of these phenomena is discussed.

articleTitle: Scattering Modeling of Micro-rough Surface SAR Target Based on Hybrid Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The scattering target model of micro-rough surface SAR, based on the physical optics method, cannot calculate incoherent scatter component, it is proposed the SAR target scattering model, established by hybrid method with physical optics and small perturbation method. The former was for calculating the coherent component, the latter was for the incoherent component. Experiment shows that the SAR target scattering model, based on hybrid method, can effectively solve the incoherent scattering component calculation of micro-rough surface SAR target.

articleTitle: Parallel Computing Graphene Frequency Selective Surface (GFSS) with Large Finite Array Using HIE-FDTD Method on High Performance Computer
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Parallel computing of graphene frequency selective surface (GFSS) with large finite array is performed using hybrid implcit-explcit finite-difference time domain (HIE-FDTD) method. Such GFSS consists of N*N units, where N is an arbitrary integral number. For example, even as N is small as 50, the FDTD cells generated for computing can be still as high as 3.5 billions. With the help of high performance computer (HPC), our computed GFSS with large finite array can achieve two passband operating at Terahertz bands. On the other hand, thanks to the unique feature of graphene, the central frequency of each passband can be adjusted by changing the graphene chemical potential or applied electrical or magnetic field, as demonstrated numerically.

articleTitle: Unconditionally Stable TDFEM Algorithm Based on “Brick” Element
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The basic theory of an unconditionally stable time domain finite-element method (US-TDFEM) based on the “brick” element is elaborated. Starting from the matrix equation of traditional TDFEM (T-TDFEM), the high-order modes that cause instability are deleted, and a new matrix equation is obtained, and then the iterative calculation is performed in time domain. As a result, the US-TDFEM can use a larger time step that is only determined by the upper frequency of the input signal. The resonant frequencies of the cavity with a small deformation and the cavity filled with a non-uniform dielectric are calculated. The numerical results demonstrate the good performance of this method in the calculation of the resonant frequencies of resonators with fine features.

articleTitle: Compensation of Ionospheric Phase Scintillation of ALOS PALSAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: By using the data of Phase Array L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR) on board Advanced Land Observing Satellite (ALOS), this paper shows the compensation of ionospheric phase scintillation. The phase scintillation is generated based on the multiple phase screen theory and added into the PALSARL1.0 data (unfocused raw data). The Phase Gradient Autofocus (PGA) is then applied to remove the phase distortion. Simulations show that after compensation, the effects of ionospheric phase scintillation is obviously removed.

articleTitle: Investigation on Ship LEMP Protection Design and Test
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Lightning strike and electromagnetic induction resulted from lightning pose a serious threat to the electronic equipment and weapons on the naval ship. Systematic protection design is therefore essential to reduce the probability of electrical equipment and weapons being damaged. In this paper, we discussed the whole ship direct-lightning protection scheme, combining the installation of lightning rods on top of masts as well as the direct lightning strike protection and reinforcement of the local high structures such as ship borne medium-wave and short-wave communication antennas and large radar antennas. The design plans that developing lightning induction protection from different levels such as the platform, system, equipment or subsystem are analysed. The contents and methods of relevant verification and assessment test are also discussed.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of a Microstrip Patch based on Broadband PRRS
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband polarization rotation reflective surface (PRRS) is designed and applied to wideband radar cross section (RCS) reduction in this paper. The PRRS can convert linearly polarized incident wave to reflective wave with orthogonal polarization, and a high polarization conversion ratio (PCR) can be achieved across a broad band. When the PRRS is arranged with in a chessboard configuration and placed around a microstrip patch, the monostatic RCS of the microstrip patch can be reduced 8dB from 6.9GHz to 14.9GHz. The RCS reduction performance and principle are also analysed.

articleTitle: A Compact Wide-Band Corrugated Horn for Satellite Communicatio
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the increasing demand for telecommunications services in recent years, in order to minimize the number of antennas on spacecraft, this paper proposed a wide-band compact corrugated horn feed antenna for Broadcast Satellite Services (BSS) and Fixed Satellite Services (FSS). Simulation is done to verify the performances of the design. The simulation results indicate that the horn antenna can cover the 10.7GHz-21.2GHz frequency band with return loss less than -28 dB and the antenna has good pattern symmetry in both E-plane and H-plane with phase center stability. The proposed corrugated horn feed antenna has wide application prospects in the field of satellite communication.

articleTitle: A 2D Numerical Study of the Langmuir Parametric Instability in the Ionospheric Modification
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Parametric Decay Instability (PDI) plays an important role in the interaction of the high-power HF EM waves with ionosphere plasma. In this study, we have constructed a 2D numerical simulation model for studying PDI with a nearly realistic ionosphere background and a radio wave propagation model by taking a proper processing for the routine dynamic equations of plasma with generalized Zakharov method. The simulation results found that high-power HF EM waves could excite two electrostatic modes of a Langmuir wave and an ion acoustic wave near the reflection point of the ordinary wave (O-mode) within a timescale order of millisecond. The amplitude of density perturbation grows exponentially and significantly influencing the plasma frequency related to `low frequency' density background. These processes are also followed by plasma caviton structures and trapped Langmuir waves. Finally, the O-mode heating leads to an intense localized turbulence. This paper also presents the simulation results of Langmuir parametric instability (LPI) excited by powerful HF wave heating at the O-mode reflection height. The study of this article contributes to formation of a deep impression for the physical mechanism of the Parametric Decay Instability (PDI). It is also helpful to research on the nonlinear interaction between the high-power HF EM waves and ionosphere plasma.

articleTitle: Design of A Broadband Vertically Polarized Omnidirectional Array Based on Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using eight Vivaldi elements, a wideband omnidirectional array is proposed in this paper. First, in order to achieve roundness radiation pattern of array in horizontal plane, a Fermi Vivaldi antenna is optimized, which can achieve a 3-dB beam width of 45° (±10°) from 5.5GHz to 7.6GHz. Then, the elements in the H-plane with periodic angle of 45° are employed to build the circular array. Finally, the array is fabricated and its performance is evaluated. Measured result shows the designed array can obtain a bandwidth from 5.5 to 7.6GHz for both omnidirectional radiation pattern and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤ -10 dB. In addition, this array has a potential application for beam switching with smooth angular variation over a 360° range.

articleTitle: Zonal Variation Features of Low-Latitude Ionospheric Electron Density Observed by Swarm Constellation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to investigate the features of the zonal direction variation of low-latitude ionospheric electron density (Ne) at the altitude above the ionospheric F2 peak, Ne measurements probed by the lower pair of Swarm constellation from 17 April 2014 to 31 December 2017 have been analyzed. We found that in most cases the zonal direction variation of low-latitude Ne over a zonal separation of about 150 km can be ignored during local daytime. However, during 19:00-04:00 LT, i.e., local night, significant zonal direction variations of low-latitude Ne were often observed (with the occurrence rate of 12.49%) over the zonal separation of about 150 km, which were primarily induced by the presence of equatorial plasma irregularities (EPIs). The annual occurrence rate of significant zonal direction variations of low-latitude Ne decreased with the decreased solar activity during 2014-2017. Our findings show that under high solar activity condition significant zonal variations of low-latitude Ne took place frequently at local night over a zonal separation of about 150 km because of the presence of EPIs, which means regional forecasting (namely, Ne measurements observed over one location is used to predict that over another nearby location) may be a futile endeavor at night during high solar activity years.

articleTitle: Rocket-induced Daytime Midlatitude Plasma Depletions Observed by Swarm Constellation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The occurrence of ionospheric daytime midlatitude plasma depletions (DMLPDs) is a rare phenomenon because of the expected refilling of plasma depletions by photoionization during daytime. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket delivered an Earth observation satellite to orbit from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California at 18:51 UT on 24 August 2017. About 58 min after the rocket launch, DMLPDs were detected near the launch site by Swarm A and Swarm C satellites, i.e., the lower pair of the Swarm constellation. These DMLPDs were observed at an altitude of about 470 km (above the ionospheric F2 peak) within 25°N-40°N geographic latitude, corresponding to approximately 30.7°N-45.5°N geomagnetic latitude. The formation of these DMLPDs is difficult to explain in association with natural phenomena. The appearance of these DMLPDs near the launch station (with a geographic longitude separation of about 2.6°) about 58 min after the rocket launch strongly suggests that they were induced by the rocket launch. The characteristics of these DMLPDs identified from the in situ plasma measurements are (1) enhancement in electron temperature, (2) reduction in electron pressure, and (3) absence of electron density substructures.

articleTitle: Research on Non-uniform Nested Grid FDTD Method Based on Ionospheric Zakharov Model
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper, based on plasma generalized Zakharov model in ionosphere, studies the non-uniform nested grid in FDTD algorithm under plasma background. It is used to improve the FDTD algorithm for studying the nonlinear process of the ionospheric Langmuir disturbance. A non-uniform nested grid method which can reduce the computational complexity of explicit FDTD algorithm while guaranteeing the computational accuracy is studied. A non-uniform nested grid FDTD method for calculating electromagnetic problems involving different orders of magnitude is proposed. Finally, the correctness and superiority of the non-uniform nested grid are verified by simulating the electromagnetic field distribution and propagation characteristics of the ionospheric Langmuir disturbance.

articleTitle: The Effect of Earth Curvature on the Full-wave Model
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The full wave method is a computationally-efficient model to solve electromagnetic field of the very low frequency wave in three-dimensional space of the horizontally-stratified medium. When the signal wave propagates further lateral distance from the source, the effect of earth curvature cannot be neglected. We modify the full wave model via considering the effect of earth curvature. Comparing with the planar-stratified model and satellite data, we find that the energy distribution computed by the spherical-stratified model is more compact.

articleTitle: Simulation of Density Decay of Rocket Exhaust Plume with Solid and Neutral Gas Mixture Production
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on hydrodynamic equation, particle orbital motion theory and dust charging theory, we present simulation method for ionosphere electron density depletion caused by neural gas release and dust grains injection, respectively. Neural gas injection will form an isotropic decay structure, while small-scale dust particles injection will form a “bundle” tail structure. Finally, we get the complex ionospheric trail characteristics of “squid-like” structure, which is of great significance to understand the physical mechanism of modified space plasma.

articleTitle: New Measurement Methods of Dust Charge Based on Infrared Extinction Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The dust charge is a very important physical quantity and it needs to be measured accurately to understand the physical characteristics of dusty plasma. Through analyzing the simulated charged dust extinction signal, a new method to measure the dust charge quickly and without interference is sought. The result shows that the scattering mechanism in the far infrared band is low in absorption efficiency, it is necessary to increase the power attenuation by multiplying the light path to realize the measurement of dust charge, the upper limit of allowable particle size is 1 μ m. Resonance absorption mechanism in the middle infrared band, however, increases its absorption efficiency by 4 orders of magnitude, which allows the dust charge measurement with the spectral analysis method according to the dispersion effect in addition to the power attenuation method, the spectral resolution of single charge is 0.01cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The feasibility of measurement dust charge based on infrared extinction theory is shown theoretically.

articleTitle: An UWB Antenna with Broad Beamwidth and Dual-circular-polarization Performance
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a four-fed metallic antenna with two feeding networks, which has switchable dual-circular-polarization performance in an ultra wide frequency band, is presented. The antenna is an improvement of a slot patch antenna, combining broadband feeding structure and metal ground structure for parasitical radiation. The feeding network is composed of two three-ports 180°phase-shifters and a low profile 3dB 90°-hybrid coupler chip. This antenna achieves circular polarization switching by hybridizing two 180°phase-shifters with 90° phase difference between their inputs. The antenna is designed and optimized to cover X band(8-12GHz).

articleTitle: Research on Simplified Model of Spaceborne Early-warning Radar Clutter Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to simulate the spaceborne early-warning radar echo, a clutter simulation model is proposed. In spaceborne radar clutter simulation, the problem of two-dimensional widening in the range-Doppler domain of traditional simplified model is analyzed, as a result of beyond the precondition of the conventional airborne clutter simulation model. For the spaceborne condition, a new simplification is proposed. Taking into account the accuracy and efficiency of the simulation, a simplified spaceborne warning radar clutter model is proposed. The simulation results show that the new model improves the accuracy of the clutter simulation compared with the traditional one, and the simulation efficiency is taken into account as well.

articleTitle: A Bi-iterative Model Electromagnetic Scattering from a Ship Floating on Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper the composite scattering from a perfectly electric conducting (PEC) ship floating on sea surface is investigated by a bi-iterative physical optics (PO) method. In present method both the scatterings of partially buried ship and underlying sea surface are calculated by the PO method. And a bi-iterative strategy is considered, including the mutual interaction among points on ship in direct scattering and the mutual interaction between ship and sea surface in coupling scattering. In addition, the coupling interaction between partially buried ship and sea surface contains two parts: (1) the upper surface of sea surface and the upper part of ship; (2) the lower surface of sea surface and the lower part of ship. In numerical simulations, the bistatic normalized radar cross section (NRCS) of the composite model are computed by the bi-iterative PO method and are compared with those by the conventional method of moments (MOM). The results show the proposed method has a good accuracy and can greatly reduce the computational time and memory requirement.

articleTitle: Statistical Estimation of Uncertainty in Surface Duct Parameters Inversion
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The tropospheric duct parameter inversion problem using the global optimization algorithm to find the optimal value of the objective function is a typical point estimation problem. In some cases, we need not only the best estimate of the refractive profile, but also the probability problem of the most advantageous, that is, the uncertainty of the inversion. Therefore, this paper uses Bayesian theory to calculate the uncertainty of the statistics of duct profile parameters. However, since the parameter vector dimension is high, the posterior probability density of each parameter cannot be directly calculated. Therefore, an efficient sampling algorithm is needed to sample the parameter vector. We used the Metropolis-Hasting sample in the MCMC sampling algorithm to sample the profile parameters and obtained a good statistical result.

articleTitle: Modeling of GPS Signal Propagation in Tropospheric Duct on Spherical Rough Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the low-elevation GPS signal propagation characteristics in tropospheric environment on spherical rough sea surface, this paper revises the initial field model of parabolic equation for GPS signal propagation on spherical, rough and impedance sea surface, focusing on the diffuse scattering of GPS signal on rough sea surface. By comparing with the traditional initial field model under the condition of plane, smooth and conductor sea surface, it is shown that the modified model can describe the GPS initial field distribution more realistically, and based on the modified initial field model, the spatial propagation power distribution of low-elevation GPS signal in the tropospheric duct is calculated.

articleTitle: The Two-Dimensional Fusion Imaging method based on Iteration Dictionary Bayesian Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The technology of multi-radar fusion imaging is proposed by Lincoln laboratory in 1990s, which can markedly improve the quality of imaging by the two-dimensional fusion of frequency spectrum and azimuth. But the application is severely restricted by the estimation precision of incoherent parameter in multi-radar which relies deeply on the signal to noise ratio (SNR). An algorithm of iteration dictionary Bayesian parameter estimation is proposed in this paper, which amends the traditional Bayesian estimation by the weighted clustering and parameter zooming, and the simulation indicate its availability in abating the dependency of SNR.

articleTitle: Laser Range Profile Base on Convolution of Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The LRP reflects the shape of the target surface and the material properties by acquiring the radial dimension of the target. However, it has been found that by changing the emission pulses, the LRPs by the same target may be different. In addition, different targets may acquire the same LRPs. It makes difficult to identify the target by using LRP. This paper proposes a method base on convolution of time domain, which can solve this problem well.

articleTitle: Dependence of Altitudes of HFPL and HFIL on Electron Temperature during Ionospheric Heating
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the altitude characteristics of the high frequency pump enhanced ion line (HFIL) and plasma line (HFPL) during an ionospheric heating campaign with a pump frequency near the fifth gyro-harmonic at the EISCAT. Those UHF observations show that the observing altitude of the HFIL and HFPL varies as a function of pump frequency. In conclusion, the altitude variations of the HFIL and HFPL are essentially due to the thermal effect induced by the ionospheric heating.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Electromagnetic Band-Gap Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a compact dual-band and dual-polarized Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) structure. The unit cell is composed of an inner folded rotated Jerusalem cross cell and four outer T-shaped cells. All of cells are connected with ground by via. The inner resonance cell operates in low frequency band, and outer resonance operates in high frequency band. Different frequency ratios can be obtained by adjusting the dimensions of inner and outer resonance cells. The greatest advantage of this EBG is that the adjustable range of frequency ratio is very wide. Additional results will be presented during the symposium.

articleTitle: Effect of Cylindrical and Spherical Conformation on Transmission Characteristics of FSS
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The influence of cylindrical conformation and spherical conformation with 20×20 and 7×7 FSS unit cells respectively is analyzed in this paper. The wideband metallic FSS has a passband between 9-11 GHz and has the potential to be bend. HFSS is used for searching the optimum dimension of the FSS unit cell and simulating the conformation system. We analyze the transmission property, current distribution successively and explain the phenomena such as fringe effect.

articleTitle: Study of spatial characteristics of artificial field aligned scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Artificial field-aligned irregularities (AFAI) induced by ionospheric heating has the property of artificial field-aligned scattering (AFAS) to incident wave, which can be used in long distance VHF transmissions. According to the physical model of AFAS, a calculation model has been deduced for the available area supporting AFAS transmission for a given heating station. Simulation results show that the available area increase with decreasing inclination, what means a great advantage for mid- and low-latitude in AFAS transmissions. The results also show that, with the increasing height, the available area increase, decrease and have a maximum value while the inclination less than 66°, large than 71°, and between 66° and 71° respectively. These results can be used in selection of the heating location, terminals and parameters in AFAS transmission applications.

articleTitle: Lateral Optical Binding of Stratified Biological Cells Induced by High-Order Bessel Beams
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the generalized multi-particle Mie equation (GMM) and Electromagnetic Momentum (EM) theory, the lateral binding force (BF) exerted on stratified biological cells induced by an arbitrary polarized high-order Bessel beam (HOBB) is investigated with particular emphasis on the half-conical angle of the wave number components. The illuminating HOBB with arbitrary polarization angle is described in terms of beam shape coefficients (BSCs) within the framework of generalized Lorenz-Mie theories (GLMT). Different types of cells, including a real Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell and a lymphocyte which are respectively modeled by a coated and five-layered sphere, are studied. Numerical effects of various parameters such as beam polarization angles, incident wavelengths, particle sizes are numerically analyzed in detail. The observed dependence of the separation of optically bound particles on the incidence of HOBB is in agreement with earlier theoretical prediction. Accurate investigation of BF induced by HOBB could provide an effective test for further research on BF between more complex particles, which plays an important role in using optical manipulation on particle self-assembly.

Index Terms: Increase In The Number Of Layers

articleTitle: A Study on Evaluation Detection Performance of HF Surface Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Different from the conventional microwave radar, HF radar working environment is terrible. There are many factors effect on the detection performance, and most of them associated with the radar operating frequency, so it's very important to select a proper operating frequency for HF radar. Based on the radar equation, detailed analysis of factors which associated with the performance of radar is showed, including the radar parameters, environmental parameters and target characteristics.

articleTitle: Meridional Direction Features of Equatorial and Low-Latitude Plasma Depletions Observed by Swarm Satellites
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions is an important space weather phenomenon, which often produce severe ionospheric scintillations. According to the well-known formation mechanism of the equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions, i.e., the generalized Rayleigh-Taylor (RT) instability mechanism, these plasma depletions are expected to occur mainly at night and appear simultaneously at the geomagnetic conjugate locations in the northern and southern hemisphere. Although many studies on the equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions have been performed in recent years, there are few reports on the variation features of the equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions along the geomagnetic meridian direction. In this study, we have analyzed in situ electron density measurements obtained by the three Swarm satellites in the 55°E-155°E geographic longitude (GLON) sector during the equinox months of high solar activity years, i.e., February-April 2014, September-November 2014, February-April 2015, and September-November 2015. We found that the equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions were observed mainly at night, which are consistent with the statements of the generalized RT instability mechanism. Moreover, we found that in most cases the appearance of the equatorial and low-latitude plasma depletions presented the north-south hemisphere symmetry. However, sometimes (with the occurrence rate of ~16-27%) they presented the north-south hemisphere asymmetry, namely, they were only detected at the low-latitude region in the northern hemisphere or southern hemisphere, which cannot be explained by the generalized RT instability mechanism.

articleTitle: Microwave technology used for plasma diagnostic in complicated situations
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the microwave technology has been applied to measure the plasma parameters in large-volume AC glow discharge with coaxial gridded hollow electrodes. By measuring the phase shift of microwave through the plasma, the characteristics of the plasma density changing with the input power in hollow ac discharge plasma has been confirmed. The phase shift of the microwave is determined by vector network analyzer (PNA-N5234A) with antennas, and the selected microwave frequency is 30GHz. Then, the experimental results are compared with the theoretical results and are in good agreement. Additionally, using the improved probe technology, the plasma parameters also are obtained by probe diagnostics. And the probe results are compared to the microwave technology, which indicates that in the AC glow discharge the microwave diagnostic is more stable and accurate.

articleTitle: CPR Modeling for Mini-RF Data Study on Lunar PSR Region
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Searching for water ice in the lunar media has been a key issue in the Moon explorations. Missions of Mini-SAR and Mini-RF SAR made compact-pol(polarization) measurements on lunar polar permanent shadowed region (PSR). High circular polarization ratio (CPR) data and two-layer model were applied to studying if water-ice in PSR could be retrieved. However, it has been studied that high CPR is not simply due to the presence of water-ice. We point out that the Campbell model is a degenerated half-space model, which confused dielectric inversion of Mini-RF data. In this paper, our numerical BART (Bi-directional Analytic Ray Tracing) is applied to simulate high-order scattering from the lunar rough surface with- and without-stone-scatters, the CPR is numerically simulated and analyzed. Furthermore, a two-layer model of KA surface (Kirchhoff-approximation)/SPA subsurface (small perturbation approximation) subsurface is developed to take account of all these topographic factors for PSR dielectric inversion. The Mini-RF data on the PSR of Hermite-A crater in the North pole (see Fig. 1) are employed for the inversion. Our results do not support previous conclusions based on the half space model, suggesting that the inversion of Mini-RF are not so straight forward in proving water-ice existence in the PSR media. It points out that double and high-order scattering of random volumetric scatters on the lunar surface can play a certain role, and high-resolution measurements and more elaborate modeling are needed for further studies.

articleTitle: Assessment of the shadow zone caused by the atmospheric duct for the shipboard radar and the measures of filling the shadow zone
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The atmospheric duct is an abnormal refraction in the atmosphere of the troposphere; it can change the normal propagation characteristics of the electromagnetic wave, so that the propagation energy of the electromagnetic wave is redistributed and the over-the-horizon detection of the ship-borne radar can be achieved on sea, at the same time the shadow zone of the shipboard radar can be caused by the atmospheric duct. In this paper, by using “the detection probability distribution method of the radar electromagnetic wave”, we evaluate the distribution of the shadow zone caused by the atmospheric duct. Furthermore, according to the different frequency radar, we analyze the distribution of the shadow zone for the s-band and c-band and x-band radar under the environment of the different atmospheric duct respectively, and the measures of filling the shadow zone are given for the shipboard radar.

articleTitle: A Near-field Perforated Dielectric Phase-Correcting Structure for Fabry-Perot Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A perforated dielectric phase correcting structure (PCS) for increasing gain of the Fabry-Perot resonator antennas (FPRAs) is presented. In the near field of the typical FPRA, the aperture phase distribution is strongly non-uniform, which significantly affects its radiation performances including gain and aperture efficiency. In order to transform such phase distribution to a nearly uniform phase distribution, a perforated dielectric PCS was proposed. The phase correction is controlled by changing the radius of the air-drilled holes in the superstrate placed over the FPRAs at the design frequency of 11GHz. A good impedance matching is achieved over 10.8-11.5GHz and the antenna also achieves a 5.9-dBi gain enhancement at 11GHz.

articleTitle: A High-conversion PW-SW Converter Based on Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-conversion converter is proposed, which uses the phase gradient metasurface (PGM), and can achieve efficient mutual conversion between spatially propagating waves (PW) and surface waves (SW). Simulations show that the converter has a PW-SW conversion of 99.99%, at 7.5 GHz, 0.09% higher than that of the similar type of designs available.

articleTitle: The Fusion Method of Sea Clutter Amplitude Distribution Model
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the situation of high resolutions, high sea states and small grazing angles, the sea clutter amplitude distribution has heavy trailing part, this part has a significant impact on the sea surface target detection. This paper introduces a fusion method of sea clutter amplitude distribution model, based on which new amplitude distribution models of sea clutter can be designed, and thus the trailing part of the sea clutter amplitude distribution can be well fitted. Through the verification by using the sea clutter data of UHF, L, and S-band, it is indicated that the introduced fusion method can give a better fit in the trailing part of the sea clutter amplitude distribution than other conventional modeling methods. Further, for the amplitude distribution without heavy trailing part, this method also has a good fitness.

articleTitle: Diurnal Variations of Ionospheric Electron and Ion Temperature with Altitude measured by EISCAT Svalbard Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The EISCAT Svalbard Radar (ESR) provides the measurement of the electron and ion temperature in the polar ionosphere, which is of scientific merits to investigate its energetics variations. Statistical analysis of ESR electron and ion temperature data during the high solar activity years of 2001-2002 was performed. The results as follows: The diurnal and altitude variation of electron and ion temperature is very similar. From the perspective of diurnal variation, they both have the characteristic phenomenon of morning overshoot, daytime valley and evening enhancement.
