These features show larger values at higher altitudes. Otherwise, when the electron temperature is larger than 1200K, the electron temperature decreases with the increase of electron density.

articleTitle: The Experimental Results from SURA HF Facility and CSES Satellite
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Since June 2018, SURA heating facility in Russia has carried out the experiments in emitting high frequency (HF) radio waves with O-mode and disturbing the ionosphere, together with the in-orbit satellite of China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES). By collecting the observing data onboard CSES including electric field, in-situ plasma parameters and energetic particle flux, the results show that in local daytime no pumping waves were detected by the electric field detector (EFD) on CSES even the emitted power reaching 90 MW, and no any obvious plasma disturbances were observed from CSES. While in local nighttime, the pumping waves were clearly distinguished in HF-band electric field at the emitted frequency with the emitted power only 30MW, in which the power spectrum density of electric field was larger than the normal background to an order of magnitude, with the propagating radius exceeding 200 km. This joint experiment of SURA-CSES illustrates that, CSES can cross SURA facility within a quite near distance with present designed orbit, which can insure the effective heating time from SURA and make CSES most possibly to observe the perturbations at the topside ionosphere excited by SURA.

articleTitle: Investigation of Planar Parasitic Technique of the Printed Dipole
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel printed dipole antenna with high gain and wide band is proposed where the planar parasitic technique is used. This antenna consists of a printed dipole and an asymmetrical rectangular frame on the same layer surrounding the dipole in order to get the maximal radiation in the vertical direction of the plane by coupling the energy from the dipole, and the corresponding substrate is Wangling'sF4B. Consequently, the omnidirectional radiation character is changed into the bidirectional radiations similar to the slot antenna. The simulation results show that the resonance is affected few in the new design compared with the conventional printed dipole, but both the bandwidth and the gain are enhanced obviously. That is, the improved bandwidth is 20.3% compared with 13.5% of the conventional one, and the gain of the convectional dipole antenna is 2.05-2.13dB in the 10dB band 2.35-2.69 GHz while it is 3.6-6.1dB in the band 2.30-2.82GHz of the proposed one. And as well the simulated and measured S11s are compared and analyzed in the end.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Echo Characteristics in One-Dimensional Inhomogeneous Plasma Sheath
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The “black-out” phenomenon of reentry vehicles has been a bottleneck problem that has plagued people for many years. Based on the basic interaction mechanism between electromagnetic wave and plasma, researchers have carried out a series of studies in order to overcome the “blackout” phenomenon essentially, and solving the Communication between Reentry Vehicle and ground radar station. In this paper, the shift operator finite difference time domain (SO-FDTD) method is applied to calculate the echo amplitudes of one-dimensional inhomogeneous plasma sheath in time and frequency domain. The physical mechanism of plasma sheath and electromagnetic (EM) wave is elaborated by analyzing the echo characteristics of EM wave, which provides some meaningful reference for the study of plasma sheath and target monitoring.

articleTitle: A Domain Decomposition Method Based on Volume-Surface Integral Equation for complex Dielectric/Metallic Composite Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel non-overlapping and non-conforming domain decomposition method (DDM) based on volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) is presented for the electromagnetic analysis of complex Dielectric/Metallic Composite Targets. In this scheme, such composite objects are decomposed into multiple composite subdomains. To model efficiently subdomains involving very thin dielectric, the VSIE with simplified prism vector (SPV) basis functions is applied. Further, a discontinuous Galerkin volume integral equation method (DG-VIE) is used for conformal as well as non-conformal volume discretizations. For PEC parts, a discontinuous Galerkin surface integral equation approach is utilized. Several numerical examples are reported to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the presented method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Distribution in Building Illuminated with Airborne Antenna Array by Using a Half-space FDTD
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the analysis of electromagnetic characters around the buildings, the effects of ground are non-ignorable. To solve the problem, a half-space FDTD method with nonuniform meshes is proposed in this paper. Two 1-D modified FDTD equations have been employed to set TF/SF boundary of the infinite half-space electromagnetic problems, then the half space problem can be solved in finite space. A method with non-uniform meshes is applied to reduce the calculation time and meshes of the building with an electrically large structure. Finally, the electromagnetic fields in Building which illuminated by the airborne antenna array is analysed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bistatic Scattering Characteristics of Vegetation in Clusters
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces the scattering theory of double-layer cluster vegetation model, and simulates the scattering coefficient of cluster vegetation by Monte-Carlo simulation method, and analyzes the bistatic scattering characteristics of cluster vegetation under different conditions.

articleTitle: Analytical Derivation of the Ellipsoid Conformal PML for Electromagnetic simulations
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new 3-D ellipsoid conformal perfectly matched layer PML is proposed and realized by the Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain (DGTD) method. The interface between free space and the PML region is an ellipsoid in this scheme. The analytical formulas are derived from differential geometry. Numerical results show that compared with planar PML, the ellipsoid PML avoid the corner problem and provides an efficient absorbing boundary condition (ABC) for DGTD simulation, Meanwhile, this new ellipsoid PML scheme has higher accuracy than that of the old ellipsoid PML scheme we've proposed.

articleTitle: Research on method of extraction elevation angle from backscatter ionogram
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using the short-wave two-dimensional antenna array, the high-frequency (3MHz~30MHz) backscatter sweep-elevation ionogram is obtained for the first time in China. Combining genetic algorithm and Otsu method, the signal region is extracted from the group path-frequency-energy three-dimensional ionogram, and the discrete point noise is eliminated by the connected domain labeling method. The Canny operator is used to obtain the nearest and farthest group path of the echo signal distribution corresponding to each frequency. On the group path-frequency-elevation three-dimensional ionogram, the elevation angle-group path distribution data of the corresponding frequency is acquired to obtain the elevation angle-group path point. The points are fitted by linear curve fitting, logarithmic fitting of the elevation angle, and logarithmic fitting of the group path. Finally, the error analysis of the fitted curve is carried out by the ionospheric data of the Qingdao Station. The results show that the curve obtained by logarithm fitting the group distance is in good agreement with the target curve.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement Technique for Dipole Combining with Cavity and Aperture Radiations
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: According to the limitation of column of the practical project, a technique of enhancing the gain and the band for the printed antenna is proposed in this paper. Here, both the cavity and the aperture radiation techniques are used to enhance the gain, and the parasitic strips above the dipole to broaden the bandwidth. This proposed antenna includes four parts, the dipole is printed on the substrate, a cavity is placed below the dipole, and another cavity with longer diameter and higher height is put outside the previous one, then the parasitic strip on the substrate is located above the dipole. The simulation results show that the resonance is affected few, but both the bandwidth and the gain are enhanced obviously. That is, the improved bandwidth is 31.8% compared with 21.7% of the conventional one, and by means of aperture radiation of the outer cavity, the gain is improved at least 1dB in the whole band, the biggest is 2.5dB comparing with the maximum of the antenna with one cavity and up to 13.6dB.

articleTitle: The Microwave Absorbing Performance of Co2+ - Ti4+ Co-doped Barium Ferrite Ceramics

articleTitle: Electron Beam Excited Surface Plasmon Polaritons Carrying Orbital Angular Momentum
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method to generate surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) is proposed. Here the electrons beam is rotating around the nanowire as well as going along it at the same time. As the trace of the electron beam is chiral, the SPP it generate can be chiral as well, enabling it to carry OAM with specific topological charge, on condition that the speed of electron matches the phase speed of light. When multiple synchronous electron sources exist, electromagnetic modes whose symmetry match that of electron sources can be additionally strengthened, possible increase the suppression ratio to other modes.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Analytical Expression for Far Radiation Field of Arbitrarily Oriented Dipole above Layered Half Space
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using the frequency-domain far field analytical expression of the arbitrary orientation dipole above the layered half space, combined with the frequency-domain to time-domain conversion relationship and the Fourier transform, the time-domain far field analytical expression is derived. The far field analytical expression contains the convolution of the incident source and the time-domain reflection coefficient. The method has clear physical concept and simple calculation, and has the advantage of obtain wide frequency band information with Fourier transform. The numerical results prove the validity and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Electricalthermal Coupling Numerical Method for Inhomogeneous Medium Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a FEM-based algorithm for calculating the electrothermal coupling process with inhomogeneous conductivity is presented. Firstly, electrothermal coupling problems are analyzed and corresponding coupling equations are presented. Secondly, iterative solution procedures are used to solve the coupling equations. Then, treatments for handling inhomogeneous problems are proposed. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to validate the efficiency of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Local Power Estimation in High-Speed Railway Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Local power estimation is essential in high-speed railway (HSR) communications. By applying the Lee's criteria and correlated shadow fading in HSR environments, we derive the lower and upper bounds of the averaging length (AL) in Ricean fading for the f rst time. With real measurement data, we f nd that the AL should be selected from about 12 to 72 wavelengths and the required sampling number changes from 28 to 88 in typical HSR scenarios. Moreover, by this method, the conf dence level is improved up to 99%. Finally, the impact of mobility on local power estimation is studied. It is found that sampling time monotonically decreases with the increase of train's speed.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-band dual-sense circularly polarized slot antenna design. The dual-band is achieved using a single-layer bended microstrip-fed configuration coupled to two slots. The dual-sense circularly polarization is obtained by an asymmetric slot-ring and L-shaped microstrip-fed in a wide square slot. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna has good circular polarization characteristics for left-hand circularly polarization (LHCP) in the lower band and right-hand circularly polarization (RHCP) in the upper band. The 10dB return loss impedance bandwidths for the lower and upper band are 14.7% and 28.4% respectively. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 8.8% and 4.5% for the lower and upper band respectively.

Author Keywords: left-hand circularly polarization (LHCP)/right-hand circularly polarization (LHCP)/ slot antenna

articleTitle: The Nonlinear Propagation of Terahertz Wave in Plasmas
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The nonlinear propagation of a terahertz wave with Gaussian beam in plasma has been investigated in this paper. The nonlinearities of pondermotive force on electron and the relativistic oscillation of the electron mass are used to study the effects on the propagation of terahertz wave in plasmas. In the present theoretical investigation, the common parabolic equation approach under the paraxial ray theory and WKB method have been adopted. Then the nonlinear differential equation for the beam-width parameter has been established and solved numerically. The numerical results show that the ponderomotive force on electron and the relativistic oscillation of the electron mass cause the periodic self-focusing/defocusing of terahertz wave. Additionally the parameteric effects on the variation of terahertz beam width parameter have been presented graphically and discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis Method of Circular Waveguide TM01 Mode Converter on the Basis of Microwave Network
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To accurately measure the performance of overmoded devices used in high-power microwave systems, a novel structure that effectively converts the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode in a rectangular waveguide to a high-purity TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode in a circular waveguide is proposed. The scattering matrix technique was used to study the mode converter along with the microwave network analysis method, obtaining some generalizations of the input port reflection and conversion efficiency which were verified by the numerical full-wave simulation. Based on the theoretical analysis, an X-band TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode generator is designed and measured. Low-power tests show that, when the length of the tuner increases from 5.7 to 11.7 mm, a wide frequency tuning range of ~500 MHz is obtained with a conversion efficiency of ~99%. Measured results and the theoretical analysis are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A Novel Spark Plug with High Field Intensity
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel spark plug with high field intensity has been designed with resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz in this paper, which is applied to auto microwave ignition for replacing traditional spark plugs. According to the electric coupling feeding theory, the electric field intensity on the top of the inner conductor was calculated as 1.25 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> through the finite element method with input power of 1 W. In that case, the threshold of plasma within the cylinder being 2.25 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> V/m will be satisfied if the input power is within 400 W. Besides, its bandwidth is 9 M, much wider than traditional microwave spark plug, which is vital for frequency drift when igniting.

articleTitle: Low Axial-ratio Circularly Polarized Antenna for Airborne Linearly Polarized Radiation Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a low axial-ratio circularly polarized array antenna with sequential rotations and progressive phase shifts of elements. The gain of the proposed antenna reaches 12.9 dB and the 3-dB beamwidth is about 45 degrees at 9.7 GHz. The axial ratio of the antenna is less than 1dB from 9.6 GHz to 9.8 GHz, and as low as 0.1 dB at 9.7 GHz. The application of the designed low axial-ratio circularly polarized antenna is able to effectively reduce polarization mismatch uncertainty which satisfies the requirement of precise airborne linearly polarized radiation measurement.

articleTitle: Hidden Markov Model Based on Target Narrow Pulse Laser Transient Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the fact that the narrow pulse laser transient characteristics of target have not been applied in target recognition, a hidden Markov model (HMM)based on transient characteristics is proposed. For the scattering characteristics of each target in different poses, the reliable model parameters of each target were completed by using the training samples, and each hidden Markov model was established. The maximum likelihood of the test samples for each model was calculated, the target feature class corresponding to the largest probability value was selected as the output category. The result shows that target recognition by hidden Markov model has better performance in terms of calculation speed and accuracy. This method is fast and effective.

articleTitle: A Domain Decomposition Method for Solving Electromagnetic Scattering from Thin Coated Metallic Multi-scale Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an integral equation-based nonconforming and non-overlapping domain decomposition (DD) method is proposed for solving electromagnetic scattering from thin coated metallic multi-scale objects. In this method, discontinuous vector basis functions are employed to expand the surface electric and magnetic currents flowing across adjacent sub-domain boundaries, and a novel interior penalty term is introduced to weakly enforce the normal continuity of these currents. This method provides an effective DD preconditioner with no need to introduce artificial touching interfaces in sub-domain models. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Dual-Frequency Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity Backed Slot Antenna Using Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-frequency substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity backed slot antenna over an Artificial Magnetic Conductor(AMC) is presented in this paper. The Artificial Magnetic Conductor is designed as a dual-band structure having an array of unit cells and operates at 7.5GHz and 12.8GHz. A circle and crisscross slot into a square metallic patch as a back-plane. By comparing the performance of the antenna loaded with AMC and without AMC. It is found that the gain of the antenna loaded with the AMC increase is obviously. The distance between the dual-frequency antenna and the AMC is 0.12λ, Improvements of front lobe to back lobe ratio are achieved as a result of using dual resonant AMC which has surface wave suppression characteristic. The simulated results show that the combination of the AMC reflector and the antenna provide directional properties at both frequency bands.

articleTitle: The Effect of Discharge Gap on Microwave Discharge
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the effect of discharge gap on microwave discharge, the paper has carried out a simulation for the particles' density distribution, conductivity distribution and the resulting frequency drift in discharge gaps of different sizes. The results show that, the smaller the gap radius and the greater the gap depth, the higher the resonance frequency; the gap size affected the change of particle concentration during the resonance process; and the parameters of resonance characteristics were different at the equilibrium time.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of V-Type Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The VHF low band (30MHz-100MHz) is a very important spectrum in radio astronomy. In this band Galactic noise is often quite strong. This thesis introduces the design and simulation of a blade-type vibrator antenna. Antenna operating in 30MHz-70MHz can satisfy the requirement of low-frequency radio observation. A blade-type vibrator antenna based on HFSS simulation software is introduced. The VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) of antenna satisfies the galaxy noise-limit condition in the working frequency band, and the antenna has the characteristics of simplicity, low cost and easy production. It's a attractive candidate for large low-frequency radio telescope arrays.

articleTitle: The Polarizer Design for CFETR High Power Millimeter Wave System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The polarization control is very important for high power millimeter wave heating experiment on CFETR. Two polarizers with different groove depths were designed in this paper. The calculated results reveal nearly arbitrary polarization wave can be obtained by employing the collaboration of two polarizers, it would ensure the proper heating mode acquisition at any beam injection angle.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Kelvin Wake of Ship Based on MPI
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An parallel small slope approximation acceleration algorithm based on MPI is improved to calculate the electromagnetic scattering of the ship's wake on the sea surface in this paper. The parallel algorithm calculates the backscattering coefficient at different angles by starting multiple processes, and can solve the electrical large scale electromagnetic scattering problem. The Kelvin wake model of the ship is established by the point source perturbation method. The Elfouhaily spectrum is adopted to construct the rough sea surface. Then the parallel small slope approximation method is used to calculate the electromagnetic scattering of the Kelvin wake produced by the ship. The electromagnetic scattering results were compared with those of pure sea surface. In addition, the effect of different wind speeds and different ship speeds on the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the ship's Kelvin wake are also discussed. The acceleration ratio of different frequencies and different numbers of samples were calculated to further verify the effectiveness of the parallel algorithm.

articleTitle: Evaluation of RF Exposure Dosimetry from a Mobile Phone Inside a Vehicle by Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether use of cell phone in a vehicle increases the risk of exposure. In this study, a simplified mobile phone with a dual-frequency inverted-F antenna was generated as a radio frequency excitation and was placed on a vehicle console. The total radiation power and electrical field distribution in the vehicle was analyzed by Method of Moment. One sitting posture realistic human model was considered as a vehicle driver. The hybrid numerical method was used to evaluate the specific absorption rate of the human body. The results indicate that (1) the total radiation power of the antenna was decreased due to the metallic structures of the vehicle frame. (2) The electric field strength and distribution were significantly changed because of the presence of the metallic vehicle frame. (3) The specific absorption rate of the human body was increased while the human using a mobile phone inside the vehicle.

articleTitle: A Compact S-band Digital T/R module in Multi-function MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact S-band transmitting-receiving (T/R) module in massive MIMO is presented in this paper. This T/R module is tile-style which consists of two layers. It includes 16 digitalized channels with digital pre-distortion (DPD) function. The DPD feature enables use of high efficiency PAs, which is beneficial for both multi-function active electronically scanned array (AESA) and the 5th generation mobile communication system (5G). The T/R module is supposed to operate in either TDD or FDD mode. This T/R module has been used in 128-channel massive MIMO for 5G system, and also it has the potential for large-scale AESA.

articleTitle: Research on Broadcast and Television Signal Power Detection System Based on Space Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadcast and television signal power detection system based on space radiation is designed in this paper. It solves the problem that the in-use broadcast and television transmitting equipment cannot be detected due to the difficulty of coordination and the lack of coupling port during the traditional conduction detection. The system is mainly composed of an antenna, a test receiver, a computer and detection software. During the detection, the system is set up at a appropriate place, and the corresponding parameters are input in to the software. The system will complete the reception, storage and calculation of the broadcast and television signals at the corresponding frequency points, and then obtain the equivalent EIRP of the transmitting port. The actual detection shows that the system is stable and the deviation is less than ± 6dB. The research improves the management level of in-use broadcast and television station by rose to a overall performance of in-use station through space radiation instead of that of the independent parts such as transmitters, feeders, and transmitting antennas.

articleTitle: Frequency Scanning Leaky-wave Antenna Based on Goubau Line Formed by Loading Parasitic Branches
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a Goubau line formed by loading parasitic branches which can function as guiding the EM wave's radiation. The whole structure consists of Goubau line and the CPW matching part which can excite the plane wave, with a thickness of 0.06λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 6.5 GHz. By loading the parasitic branches an additional amount of phase matching with the radiated waves in the air can be provided. Compared with other microstrip antennas, the monolayer structure has the advantage of easily machining in the wireless communication system. In this paper a leaky-wave antenna with working band from 4-9GHz is designed. The antenna displays a good broadside radiation function which can be demonstrated by working at even mode and odd mode. The scanning angle comes to about 60 degree. The radiation efficiency can reach to above 88% in the band.

articleTitle: Investigation on Matching Conditions of Langmuir Parametric Instability in Ionospheric Heating
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Parametric decay instability (PDI) is an important process in ionospheric heating. HFPLs and HFILs in spectra of ISR are the direct observational evidences of PDI excitation. Stimulated electromagnetic emissions (SEE), enhanced airglow and artificial ionized layer are also closely related to PDI. The focus of this talk will be on the generation of PDI and Langmuir turbulence based recent observational and simulational study. This presentation includes a few topics: (1) Recent heating experiments presented excitation of PDI during the O-mode heating period by EISCAT. We suggest that the full dispersion relationship of the Langmuir wave can be employed to analyze the O-mode parametric instability excitation. A modified kinetic electron distribution is proposed to satisfy the matching condition of parametric instability excitation. (2) The simulation results of 1D Zakharov model show that caviton collapse dominate in higher altitude area and cascade dominate in lower altitude, which is consistent with strong Langmuir theory (SLT). Based on the spectrum analysis, the development of PDI to Langmuir turbulence is investigated in details. (3) Langmuir turbulence leads to strong electron acceleration. Generation mechanism of Langmuir turbulence and electron acceleration are also discussed with the help of numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wideband Optically Transparent Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed an optically transparent antenna designed with indium tin oxide (ITO) film. ITO is a transparent material with good electrical conductivity. The antenna made of ITO material has light-transparent characteristic compared with the antenna made of traditional metal, and can be applied to special scenes such as window glass and display screen. The working frequency band of the antenna is 0.8-6 GHz. This band covers 2G, 3G, 4G and WLAN bands. The main radiator of the antenna adopts a self-complementary structure and is fed with a gradual structure, thus the antenna has ultra-wideband characteristics.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Effect of Electrode Shape on Microwave Discharge
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Given that the microwave discharge involved the discharge field strength and the discharge electrode shape of spark plugs, providing 6.77×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>V/m is the initial maximum field strength, the simulation is carried out to compare and analyze the changes in the maximum electron concentration and the conductivity between the truncated-electrode discharge and the stepped-electrode discharge, showing that the truncated electrode discharge featured much higher discharge rate and electron concentration compared with the stepped electrode discharge.

articleTitle: The design of a high gain, low profile and planar antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We proposed a patch antenna with a circular ring structure loaded at the source of antenna radiation to increase the gain. Expanding the ground to suppress the backward wave of the antenna. Compared with conventional antennas, the gain of the designed antenna is 11.6 dBi, which is increased by 5 dBi, and improved with 75.7%. The metamaterial antenna shows good impedance match in a wideband form 8.47 GHz to 9.37 GHz. This paper provides a method to improve the gain of the micro-strip patch antenna and the method can effectively improve the gain of the antenna without increasing the profile. Experiment ware carried out to verify the simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on Active Adaptive Cancellation Technology for Tight Coupling Interference
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper has explained the defects in the traditional passive adaptive cancellation technology under the tight coupling interference, introduced an active adaptive cancellation technology (AACT), and offered a mathematical model of the active adaptive cancellation system, as well as the formulae of interference cancellation ratio (ICR) and convergence time for simulation and experiment. The results show that the system is characterized by high ICR and short convergence time and that the AACT can effectively deal with the tight coupling interference and its application can expand further.

articleTitle: The Particles Releasing Process Using Injections for the Exploration of Active Space Experiment
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The techniques of Active Space Experiments (ASE) include the particles injection and electromagnetic beams emission into geospace from ground or space. Based on the mechanism of the interaction between dusty particles and plasmas in ionosphere, this paper analyses the effect of particle shape on the charge effects of plasma. The processes of superfine particles injection and particle clouds formation are also discussed. This paper presents some results from theoretical analysis, experimental results and numerical simulations. The results show that the well-organized local space structure of nanoscale slender particles cloud display scattering effect to electromagnetic waves along with stronger electron adsorption capacity. The results also show that the nanoscale particles behave the shorter relaxation time than the microscale particles and in mesosphere a particles cloud of 800 meter scale can be produced using the injections method.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional numerical simulation of arbitrary configuration and surface-modified dust particles charging process in plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We have established a three-dimensional numerical simulation method to simulate the charging process of dust particles in plasma. The method is based on Particle-in-Cell (PIC) technique, which can mesh a plasma region containing particles with arbitrary configuration. The innovative point of our method is that it can be applied to surface-modified dust particles, including electrophilic and dielectric properties modification. In addition, the boundary flow injection conditions in several typical scenarios are also considered. This method realizes a three-dimensional numerical simulation of arbitrary configuration and surface-modified dust particles charging process in plasma.

articleTitle: DM EMI Reduction using the Gate Drive Signal in a Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the miniaturization and high frequency of integrated circuits, the electromagnetic interference (EMI) which could be divided into conducted interference and radiated interference has received more and more attention. It is well-known that the conducted interference depends on common-mode current and differential-mode current flowing through the parasitic capacitance of transistors and diodes in the power circuits. In order to present the conducted noise from interfering with other systems, this paper analyses the generation principle of noise current flowing the parasitic capacitance of transistor, and introduces a new active cancellation structure which is composed by a comparator and a RC differential circuit to suppress the noise current. The active cancellation structure designed in this paper uses a simpler structure to make the differential mode conducted EMI on the power line reach a lower level. This new method is also applied to the flyback converter with the simulation result that the conducted EMI is reduced obviously.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband and Polarization-insensitive RCS Reduction Digital Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new AMC checkerboard structure is proposed to reduce radar cross section (RCS). Based on hybrid array pattern synthesis (APS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, the metasurface is optimized to obtain the diffusion scattering patterns. Compared to the equal-sized PEC surface, it can achieve more than 10 dB RCS reduction in an ultra-wide frequency from 8.16 to 18.6 GHz with 78% bandwidth for normal x- and y-polarized incidence waves. The theoretical analysis and simulation results are in a good agreement and verify the metasurface can achieve ultra-wideband and polarization-insensitive specular reflection reduction.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Ionospheric F2 Region Critical Frequency between Ionosonde Measurements and IRI-2016 Predictions over Sanya
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> region critical frequency (foF2) data collected by Sanya ionosonde (18.3°N, 109.6°E; geomagnetic: 8.39°N, 181.97°E) in 2014 have been analyzed and compared with IRI-2016 predictions using CCIR and URSI options under low geomagnetic activity conditions. We found that the peak duration of the observed foF2 values was longer in spring and autumn than that in summer and winter. Usually, the maximum of the observed foF2 appeared near 8 UT (i.e., 15 LT), and the observed foF2 had two peaks in spring and autumn. The observed foF2 values in summer were generally smaller than those in winter. Moreover, the observed foF2 values in winter were smaller than those in the equinox months. That is to say, the presence of semiannual and winter anomaly in the observed foF2 was found over Sanya in 2014. The prediction accuracy of the IRI-2016 predictions with the CCIR option and that with the URSI option are basically the same. The foF2 values predicted by IRI-2016 model are close to the observed values during daytime. However, the deviation (i.e., the absolute deviation and the relative deviation) of the IRI-2016 predicted foF2 values with respect to the observed foF2 values during nighttime is much larger than that during daytime. During nighttime, the IRI-2016 predicted foF2 values with the CCIR or URSI option underestimate or overestimate the observed foF2 values more than 50%. In general, the IRI-2016 predicted foF2 values with the CCIR or URSI option underestimate the observed foF2 values in the equinox months and overestimate the observed foF2 values in January, June and July. Therefore, our findings show that IRI-2016 model cannot predict foF2 over Sanya in 2014 very well.

articleTitle: A Algorithm of Preamble Acquisition Base on Differential Correlation Module for CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Random access process is one of the basic physical processes of uplink and downlink interaction in CDMA system. When a user terminal connects with the mobile network, the random access process must be included. Traditional direct acquisition algorithm of random access preamble signal can't detect correctly in the presence of large frequency offset. Based on the study of the generation mechanism of the preamble sequence in the upstream random access channel of WCDMA terminals, a two-step cascaded preamble acquisition algorithm based on differential correlation is proposed in this paper. The algorithm overcomes the effect of frequency offset on the performance of the preamble acquisition. The simulation results show that the algorithm has good acquisition performance for the uplink random access preamble signal of the terminal with negative signal-to-noise ratio under the condition of large frequency offset.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Ranging System Based on Reconfigurable Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The radio ranging system should meet the requirements of miniaturization and good anti-interference performance. The traditional radio ranging system is mainly based on analog circuits and works in a single ranging mode. So it's difficult to achieve system miniaturization and fight modern jammers. Using the programmable features of Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS), and the reconfigurable RF front end, we'll design a general hardware system that can works in pseudocode PM and linear FM mode. By reconfiguring the FPGA, the system can adaptively select ranging mode, working frequency band and working bandwidth. The anti-interference performance of the system is improved, and the integrated digital circuit is conducive to system miniaturization.

articleTitle: Study on Connection Boundary Conditions in Ionospheric Plasma Dispersive Media
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a method for studying the boundary conditions in ionospheric plasma dispersive media is proposed. Firstly, the Huygens principle is introduced briefly. Then the Huygens principle is introduced according to the incident source of FDTD algorithm. Finally, the boundary conditions of the plasma are modified, and the Drude model is selected to describe the dispersion characteristics of the plasma and numerical simulation. The simulation results show that the coherent error of the total field is the leakage of the scattered field, and it is verified that the modified connection boundary is correct.

articleTitle: Through-the-Wall Imaging Using Wi-Fi Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, we investigate, for the first time, the high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) through-the-wall imaging using the everyday wireless communication signals, i.e., Wi-Fi signals, in an indoor environment. We also provide physical insights into such imaging technique, which has been derived from the well-known Huygens principle. Experimentally, the data acquisition has been realized in a synthetic aperture way, and the classical back-propagation algorithm is employed to form the high-resolution imaging. Moreover, we use IEEE 802.11n protocol wireless router working at 2.4GHz, the bandwidth is 20MHz, in our experiments. It can be faithfully expected that such imaging technique can open an exciting new door for various practical applications including safety screening and others.

articleTitle: A Half-cut Microstrip Slot Antenna for Implantable Devices at ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel implantable antenna. The proposed antenna is a half-cutting of microstrip antenna printed on FR-4 substrate with size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12.4\ \mathbf{mm}\times 16 \mathbf{mm}\times 0.8\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex>. Measured bandwidth is 1.975-3.875 GHz covering ISM band.

articleTitle: Antenna automation design method based on shape blending
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: antenna radiation patterns; microstrip antennas; antenna feeds; broadband antennas; electromagnetic wave polarisation; electromagnetic wave scattering; antenna arrays; microstrip antenna arrays; microwave antennas; UHF antennas.

articleTitle: Integrated Trajectory Optimization of Multiple Aircraft under Electronic Warfare Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper deals with a new trajectory optimization modeling and algorithm for the integrated scheduling of multiple aircraft under the complex electronic warfare environment. With the cooperative flying formation of the fighter aircraft and electronic warfare aircraft, the proposed modeling and algorithm can help the flight team fulfill an optimal mission accomplishment. The effectiveness of the modeling and algorithm is demonstrated by the corresponding test case.

articleTitle: Distortion of Polarized Bessel Vortex Beams Propagation in Sandstorm
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the vector angular spectrum expansion method, distortion of polarized Bessel vortex beams in sandstorm is investigated. Assuming that the number density of sandstorm varies with the height, the model of stratified sandstorm is established. The equivalent permittivity of a stratified sandstorm in different layers is calculated by utilizing equivalent medium theory. The magnitude profiles of the reflected and transmitted field components of an oblique Bessel vortex beam incident on sandstorm are calculated and discussed. In terms of spiral spectrum expansion method, the distributions of orbital angular momentum states of the reflected and transmitted fields are obtained. This research may provide some theoretical supports for further work in exploring the potential communication applications of vortex beams in sandstorm environment.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Rainfall Rate Digital Map in China Land Area
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Rain attenuation is the main impairment for radio communication systems operating at frequencies above 10GHz, and the rainfall rate data exceeded for 0.01% of the average year are the essential data for rain attenuation prediction. Three kinds of digital maps of rain rate (mm/h) exceeded for 0.01% of the average year in China land area have been compared and analyzed herein, which are the methods in Recommendation ITU-R P.837-7, P.837-4, and the grid data produced by using the statistical data in widely distributed station in China land area. The comparison shows that the method in P.837-7 is better than previous ITU-R method, but there are still many differences between the method in P.837-7 and the grid map obtained by the local data sources in China land area.

articleTitle: Design Method of Large Power Miniaturization for Sequential Power Supply Control Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the fact that the current sequential power supply control methods can not meet the requirements of large power and small size design for the positive and negative voltage sequential power supply control circuit of the millimeter wave fuze detector power supply system at the same time, a high power miniaturization design method for the sequential power supply control circuit is proposed. The method is to design a power supply delayer in the power supply system of the millimeter wave fuze detector, so that the positive voltage can be output after a certain time delay, and the power supply system of the detector can realize the high power and miniaturization design of the sequential power supply control circuit on the basis of the negative voltage prior to the positive voltage supply. The test results show that the sequential supply of negative voltage before positive voltage can be realized effectively by using power supply delayer, and the design method of sequential supply control circuit can meet the system design requirements of high-power and small-scale.

articleTitle: Propagation of Electromagnetic Wave in a Coaxial Gridded Hollow Cathode Dusty Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of electromagnetic wave through a coaxial gridded hollow cathode helium dusty plasma was experimentally investigated. The dust particles in the plasma fell from the top of the chamber and formed a dusty plasma environment. The propagation characteristics of the electromagnetic wave were determined using a vector network analyzer with antennas in 3-5 GHz range. The measured attenuation data were in approximate accordance with the theoretically calculated curve. The experimental results showed that the charged dust particles play a significant role in the attenuation of the EM wave propagation and the dust density greatly influenced this attenuation.

articleTitle: Role of high energy precipitating particles on PMSE echoes during the simultaneous observations carried out by EISCAT VHF and UHF radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We investigate the role of precipitating energetic particles in producing PMSE echoes during the simultaneous observations conducted simultaneously by both the EISCAT VHF and UHF radars on 8 and 9 Aug 2015. Since PMSE echoes are observed even in the absence of particle precipitation in case of EISCAT VHF observations, precipitating energetic particles might be one possible reason but are not necessary for producing PMSE echoes. However, the absence of PMSE echoes during the precipitating particle precipitation in case of observations carried out simultaneously by EISCAT UHF radar shows that particle precipitation might play an important role in PMSE creation at lower frequencies.

articleTitle: The Variation Characteristics of the Spread-F Occurrences at Chongqing in China
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the post-sunset ionosphere, plasma depleted bubbles with associated irregularity structures of scale sizes varying from centimeters to kilometers are generated due to plasma instability processes which causes the ionospheric irregularities. Ionospheric spread-F was discovered some decades ago. The variation in spread-F occurrence percentages continues to be an active area for scientific investigations at the present time. The spread-F presents a large dependence on the solar flux, the local time, the season, the latitude and longitude and the magnetic disturbances. In this paper, we present simultaneous ionosonde observations carried out at Chongqing (29.51°N, 106.42°E), which is located at the middle latitude in China, to study the characteristics of spread-F occurrence percentages and variations with local time, season and solar activity during 1997 to 2016. The results show that the onset time of spread-F seems to start at around 20 LT and continue till 05 LT at middle latitude. The spread-F occurs during summer most frequently at Chongqing. The spread-F occurrences decrease with the increase of solar and geomagnetic activity at middle latitude. These observations may improve our understanding of the factors responsible for the generation, growth and dynamics of the middle latitude spread-F events.

articleTitle: Transmission Characteristics of Polarized Light in Low Visibility Fog
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Combining the parameters of the radiation fog and the transmission fog at different visibility, the depolarization characteristics of the two clouds were studied. Discuss the reflection of different fogs and the degree of polarization of transmitted light as a function of transmission distance and visibility. Found by calculation that when the visibility of the cloud is constant, the increase of the transmission distance or the decrease of the visibility of the cloud when the transmission distance is constant will enhance the depolarization effect. And usually the cloud has a stronger depolarization effect on the reflected light than the transmitted light.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Scattering from an Infinite Dielectric Periodic Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering and propagation of the periodic surface shows some special and valuable properties. In this paper, the electromagnetic scattering from dielectric periodic surface is studied. Rayleigh hypothesis, Huygens principle and Floquet theory are used to expand the scattering field by Fourier transform, and the expression of the scattering field is obtained. Based on the special structure of periodic surface, the amplitude formula of scattering field is acquired by extended boundary condition method (EBCM) and T-matrix method, and then the scattering field can be obtained. At the same time, the law of conservation of energy is used to verify the correctness of the algorithm. By studying the scattering problem of a finite periodic surface, we derive the formula for calculating the scattering cross section of an infinite periodic surface. Finally, the data of scattering cross section under different incident parameters are compared, and we can quantitatively analyze the influence of various factors on the scattering of periodic surface.

articleTitle: A UWB Label Pulse Energy Recovery Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For pulse-excited UWB antennas, because the antenna can only radiate part of the frequency energy, but the pulse signal bandwidth is very wide, a circuit for recovering energy of UWB antenna in time domain is designed in this paper. This energy recovery circuit can collect the energy wasted by the original antenna through heating, which is not radiated out, to recharge the battery, so as to achieve energy recycling and improve battery standby time.

articleTitle: Effect of Atmospheric Stability on Radio Wave Propagation in Evaporation Duct
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaporation duct is the domain propagation mechanism in the marine surface layer. This paper deals with effects of atmosphere stability on electromagnetic waves propagation in the evaporation duct environment. A popular evaporation duct model and parabolic equation method are used to model the refractivity profiles and path losses at the same evaporation duct height and seven atmosphere stable classes. Numerical results are presented to highlight the evaporation strength influence. This partly explain some experimental results where the higher signal strength corresponding under stable atmospheric conditions was observed even the duct height was not higher than the unstable atmospheric conditions.

articleTitle: A Creamer Nonlinear Ocean Surface Doppler Spectrum Simulation of a Fine Physical Model Covered by Oil Film
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the modeling of the Doppler spectrum from a time-evolving Creamer nonlinear ocean covered by oil film is presented based on a refined physical surface spectrum model of damping due to oil. The influence of oil film on the ocean surface spectrum and geometrical structure is examined briefly in the present study. On this basis, the Doppler spectra of the backscattered echo from the time-evolving Creamer nonlinear contaminated ocean are investigated in detail based on the iterative physical optics method. The Doppler spectra of the backscattered echo from clean and contaminated ocean are compared for the linear and Creamer nonlinear surfaces at various incident angles firstly. Due to the nonlinear hydrodynamics, the Doppler spectral widths of the Creamer nonlinear ocean for both clean and contaminated ocean are broader than the corresponding linear ocean counterparts as the incident angle increases. It manifests the necessity of using Creamer nonlinear model to simulate the contaminated ocean surface. Then, the simulations focus on the Doppler spectra of the contaminated rough ocean surface with different oil parameters. Simulation results show that the Doppler spectrum signatures including Doppler shift and spectral widths of the backscattered echo are affected by oil film, which are qualitatively consistent with wavetank or open ocean measurements. Furthermore, it indicates that Doppler spectrum technique is a promising tool for remote sensing of oil films floating on ocean surface.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Patch Antenna by Introduction of Capacitive Patch
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An efficient method for integrating genetic algorithm (GA) with method of moments for capacitive patch antenna design has been presented. The movement of capacitive patch within the antenna model and its length are controlled by GA in the search of the best electrical characteristics that satisfy/close to the fitting value. Method demonstrate the design of antenna and manipulation of the electrical specification of the design antenna. Antenna model was formed by right angle triangle wire grid model.

articleTitle: Short-wave line-of-sight detection system ionospheric clutter Analysis and suppression methods
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Short-wave Line-of-Sight Radar (HFLSR) is a new type radar detection system, which is used for Stealth Aircraft detection in recent years. The clutter of HFLSR was analyzed in the paper. There are three types clutter, which is ground-sea clutter, ionospheric direct reflect clutter and ionospheric back scatter clutter. It is proposed to use horizontally polarized antenna to suppress the near-surface sea clutter, suppress the direct reflection of the ionosphere by selecting the appropriate working frequency, and suppress the ionospheric return-scattering clutter by using the large time-width signal.

articleTitle: Effect of Material on Secondary Scattering of Dihedral Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the light scattering characteristics of complex targets more accurately, it is necessary to take into account the effects of secondary scattering on the overall calculation results. Since the calculation of secondary scattering is very complicated, this paper selects the simplest dihedral structure as the research target. Based on ray tracing method combined with Monte Carlo method, three typical materials including white paint, grass green paint and coated material are selected. Calculate the results of three different materials combination on the two faces of the dihedral structure, and obtain the LRCS single, secondary scattering results in three cases. It is concluded that in the dihedral structure, if one of the faces is a mirror-like material, the effect of the secondary scattering on the whole can be neglected. If it is a dihedral angle composed of a Lambertian surface or a normal rough surface, the effect of secondary scattering on the population cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lightning Induced Transient Effects on Coaxial Cables for Ships
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we study the lightning induced transient effects on coaxial cables for ships. The coaxial cables with different grounding and shielding measures are injected with lightning waves according to the US military standard MIL-STD-461G, so that the circuit voltage at the end of the cables can be detected by the oscilloscope. A simply theory analysis is given and simulations are taken to find the influence of such measures. At last, experimental measurements validate the simulation results.

articleTitle: Single-frequency and Single-sensor Three-dimensional Microwave Imaging Using Programmable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Microwave imaging based on programmable metasurface with a single sensor at single frequency has been demonstrated to be remarkably advantageous to other conventional imaging techniques due to the high-speed-data-acquisition, the low cost hardware, and the non-frequency dispersion. In this work, we establish the ambiguous function for such promising imaging paradigm, and then apply it to investigate quantitatively the performance for three-dimensional(3D) microwave imaging. Specifically, the achievable resolution is studied in terms of some influencing factors, such as the distance between probed scene and metasurface, the metasurface scale, and the coding style of metasurface. Finally, selected numerical results are provided to examine the performance of above imaging system.

articleTitle: Comparison of Spark Plugs with Different Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to improve fuel economy and combustion efficiency, high electric field is essential for designing microwave spark plugs. The higher the electric field, the larger is the plasma kernel, and the more thorough is the resulting combustion. Thus, microwave spark plug structure is vital in achieving high electric field intensity. This paper compared the effects of three different spark plug structures on the electric field. Results indicated that all of them are resonant at 2.45 GHz, thus providing useful reference for microwave spark plug design.

articleTitle: Difference Scattering Field Properties between Multilayered Defect Particles and Slightly Rough Optical Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on half-space finite difference time domain and Monte-Carlo method, composite scattering between rough optical surface and defects is investigated numerically. The defects are observed as multilayered particles for a more complex situation. In order to obtain the scattering contribution of defects, difference radar cross section is added into the calculation model of the proposed method. Selected calculations on the scattering contribution of multilayered particles or rough optical surface are analyzed in detail to demonstrate the best position to find the multilayered defects inside the optical surface is to detect in steps of a fixed degree for the incident angle.

articleTitle: Explicit and Unconditionally Stable FDTD Method for Electromagnetic Problem Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method has an important role in computational electromagnetics due to its advantages of simplicity, high efficiency, and parallelism. However, the traditional FDTD method must satisfy the CFL condition to guarantee the stability of the solution. Because of the limitation of CFL conditions, when the traditional FDTD method deals with electromagnetic problems with multi-scale structures, the time step size must be selected based on the smallest spatial grid size, and the calculation is inefficient. In this paper, an unconditionally stable FDTD method is introduced. This method takes a rectangular patch as the basic unit of space and eliminates the spatially unstable module as its basic idea. It not only retains the advantages of the traditional FDTD method's explicit iteration, but also overcomes the shortcomings associated with the time step and space step of traditional FDTD method, this method has explicit unconditional stability characteristics.

articleTitle: Study on the construction of low ionosphere physical model in mid-low latitude
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a detailed one-dimensional time-dependent ion chemistry model, which includes 23 positive ions, 11 negative ions and electronic coupled together via more than 157 reactions, physical model established in this paper calculates positive ions, negative ions and electron concentrations in ionosphere D and lower E regions. The calculations which are made by the physical model and the comparisons about the electron concentration profile with IRI-2012 (International Reference Ionosphere-2012) empirical model under the same conditions have showed. The results show that this physical model generally describes the basic characteristics of low ionosphere (60km-120km) parameters, such as the distribution of electron density with height.

articleTitle: The Efficient High Frequency Solver for Calculating the Scattered Fields from the Electrically Large Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, the fast physical optics (FPO) method is proposed to calculate the scattered fields from the coated scatterers. Different from the plane discretization, the quadratic patches are used to model the surface of the scatterers. Hence the number of the meshes would reduce greatly. With adopting the Lagrange interpolation and the closed-form formulation, the scattered fields could be represented as the analytical formulations. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and the efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: A Broadband High Efficiency Class-J Power Amplifier with a Novel Output Matching Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new method to design broadband high efficiency Class-J power amplifiers (JPAs). The wideband output matching network (OMN) is designed with a new simplified output impedance calculation method by using a two-port network. For demonstration, a broadband high efficient Class-J power amplifier based on proposed method is implemented using Cree 10-W packaged GaN HEMT devices. Measurement results show that 64%-68% drain efficiency is achieved and between 40-41.6 dBm output power with more than 10 dB gain over the frequency band of 1.2-2.6 GHz, the proposed amplifier has an ACPR between - 27.5 and -32.4 dBc over the entire band.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Two-stream Instability Induced by Equatorial Electrojet
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The equatorial ionosphere is the most active region in the Earth's space, where the E region irregularities are a common phenomenon. The two-stream instability excited by equatorial electrojet is the main reason for the formation of E-layer irregularities. The particle-in-cell (PIC) method is used in this paper to simulate the evolution process of the two-stream instability. The energy variation curve and the growth rate curve of the two-stream instability are both analyzed. In addition, the excitation strip of the instability is simply analyzed.

articleTitle: On the Predictability of FoF2 using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for forecasting the ionospheric critical frequency, foF2, one day in advance using the support vector machine approach. The output is the predicted foF2 one day ahead. The network is trained to use the ionospheric sounding data at Guangzhou station at high and low solar activity. The performance of the SVM model was verified with observed data. It is shown that the predicted foF2 has agreement with the observed foF2.

articleTitle: Brief introduction to key laboratory
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Five key Chinese research laboratories are very briefly described.

articleTitle: A Novel Non-stationary Plasma Sheath Channel Estimation and Distortion Cancellation Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new method of distortion cancellation based on channel estimation and equalization is proposed to alleviate the parasitic modulation effect of the non-stationary plasma sheath channel (PSC) on communication signals effectively. This method insert the pilot data into direct sequence spreading telemetry signals and then a novel non-stationary stochastic gradient recursive minimum mean square error (NSGR-MMSE) estimation algorithm is adopted to estimate channel states and equalize the received data at the receiving end. Different from existing mitigation strategies based on reflected signals, the main strategy in this paper is to use practical transmitted signals to mitigate the parasitic modulation effect. The proposed strategy reduces the impact of time delay and improves real-time performance. Compared with traditional minimum mean square error (MMSE) algorithm, the proposed new algorithm only needs a small amount of matrix inverse versus traditional MMSE algorithm, which reduces the computation complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed channel estimation and equalization method can improve the BER performance by three to four orders of magnitude. Moreover, the proposed NSGR-MMSE channel estimation algorithm improves the bit error rate (BER) performance about 1-2dB over the existing MMSE algorithm in the non-stationary plasma sheath channel environment.

articleTitle: Constraining interference in satellite reception and ground station receiver
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: There are different interferences in the satellite communication. A example is given in the paper, it is shown from the simulation that when using smart antenna and PASTd algorithm in the satellite communication, the radiation patterns formed by smart antenna points a main beam in the direction of the desired signal but the ability to cancel inferences.

articleTitle: Radio fuze detector reinforced by RF MEMS components
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the fact that the radio fuze detector will not work properly or even be damaged under strong electromagnetic environment, a radio fuze detector reinforced by RF MEMS components is proposed, a RF MEMS switch is integrated between VCO and the antenna, and the MEMS switch control module controls its working status according to the electromagnetic environment where the detector is located. A RF MEMS filter is integrated between the MEMS switch and the mixer to suppress out-of-band interference signals. The radio fuze detector reinforced by RF MEMS components was tested by electromagnetic impact test and ground dynamic detection test, which proved that the performance of the radio fuze detector reinforced by RF MEMS components is normal. It improves the survivability of the radio fuze detector under strong electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Ground clutter suppression: Preliminary analysis of Qujing incoherent scatter radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Incoherent scatter radar (ISR) detects the Thomson scatter echo of free electrons to inverse ionosphere parameters and is thought as the most powerful instrument to observe the ionosphere on the ground. In fact there are usually severe ground clutters around altitude 100km in the echo data. This paper introduces pulse subtraction to deal with ground clutter by using the Qujing incoherent scatter radar data. The results show that this pulse subtraction suppresses ground clutter well.

articleTitle: The Research on Life-signal Detection Based on Short-time Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The terahertz (THz) wave has the superior Doppler characteristics since it has shorter wavelength than microwave and millimeter wave (MMW). As a result, in recent years, the detection of micro-motion by means of the terahertz radar has attracted researchers' enormous interest. In this paper, a 0.22 THz radar system is built and the detection of life-signal with it is presented. Based on short-time Fourier transform (STFT), the life-signal is acquired under different breathing states. From the experimental results, the proposed method's performance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: The study of microwave scattering of anisotropic sea surface with the corrected Two-Scale model
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The high-accuracy retrieval of sea remote sensing information, such as wind field, wave height and Permittivity, is determined by the microwave scattering model at the sea surface. Thus it is meaningful to study the accurate microwave scattering characteristic of rough sea surface. Based on the current Two-Scale model, this paper modifies the model of microwave scattering from three aspects: the correction of Non-linear anisotropic sea spectrum, the correction of the joint probability density of the Non-linear anisotropic sea-surface slope and the correction of shadowing effect. It is shown by simulation that the data obtained from corrected Two-Scale model is much closer to the real experimental data than from the conventional Two-Scale model.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Hunting Property of Nearest Target Selector of Radar Seeker
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It is difficult for the current extraction and comparison target-hunting mode to be suitable for the selection of multiple targets in the offshore combat of anti-ship missiles, so the solution is hence put forward that applies the nearest-distance selector to target-hunting. Typical target-hunting situations are set to establish the target-hunting model. Explicit expression of capture probability of this nearest-distance selector is derived on the basis of reasonable simplification. The numerical simulation in typical situations demonstrates that, the performance of predetermined target-hunting is greatly improved by the distance criterion adopted in this solution, which sets the extracted multiple targets in order in terms of priority. Finally, impact extents of such factors as area of search, number of extracted objects, and target dispersion error are quantitatively evaluated. The insufficiency of using alone the method of selection of multiple nearest-distance targets is indicated with appropriate improvement actions proposed correspondingly.

articleTitle: Transmitting Coil Arrays for Improvement of Wireless Power Transmission Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) offers the promise of cutting the last cord, marking users to recharge portable electronic devices easily through the air. In the conventional transmitting coil array for wireless power transmission, an opposite magnetic field will create at the gap between the unit. Consequently, the power transfer efficiency is decreased at gap of resonator unit. To alleviate this problem, adding a coil to a conventional array to form a five-coil array structure is proposed in this article. The results show that the transmission efficiency at these locations will reach above 70%. In comparisons with the conventional system, the proposed transmitting system provides a higher wireless power transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: A novel Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Triangular Shaped Fractal Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel frequency reconfigurable antenna based on Triangular Shaped Fractal Parasitic Elements (TSFPE) has been proposed, by combining fractal techniques with frequency reconfigurable techniques. A pair of RF switches is loaded at the joint between bow-tie antenna and the TSFPE to realize frequency reconfiguration at Ku and Ka bands, and the X band can be controlled by two arms of bow-tie antenna. Simulated result shows that the proposed novel antenna has good performances in X/Ku/Ka bands.

articleTitle: Design of A Dual-band Co-aperture Microstrip/waveguide Monopulse Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low profile dual-band co-plane microstrip/waveguide monopulse antenna is designed, manufactured and tested, which is based on the development of a new microstrip line array fed at the side and a novel compact slot patch antenna with a pair of spirals. The good results of side-lobe level and radiation efficiency are presented, which is in a similar level of single band monopulse antenna. The measured result confirms the validity of this design and this antenna meets the need of dual mode compound guidance system in future.

articleTitle: The distance adjustment method of triangle-wave FM harmonic fixed range fuze
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The distance adjustment of triangle-wave FM harmonic ranging fuze is complex and difficult to implement. Aiming at this problem, the distance adjustment method of triangle wave FM harmonic fixed range fuze is proposed in this paper. The method used the adjustment of triangle wave frequency to adjust the ranging of triangle wave FM harmonic ranging radio fuze. The adjustment of triangle wave frequency changed the harmonic times and the ranging. It is proved by the simulation and actual verification that the distance adjustment method of triangle wave FM harmonic ranging radio fuze is feasible and simple. just the triangle wave frequency need to changed, other parameters are unchanged.

articleTitle: Diurnal Variation of Ionospheric Electron and Ion Temperatures with Altitude by QJISR
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
