abstract: The ionospheric plasma temperatures in March and June measured by the Qujing incoherent scatter radar have been used to study the diurnal variation of electron and ion temperatures with altitude (193-513km). It is found that there exist the morning and sunset enhancement and the daytime constant valley in electron temperature in March. The features like morning overshoot, day time valley (about 1000K) and sunset enhancement (with the maximum 3500K) show larger values at higher altitudes. The electron temperature above 1000K decreases with an increase in density. The sunset peak occurs earlier at higher altitudes. These above characteristic isn't prominent for electron temperature in June and ion temperature in all seasons. Both the electron and ion temperature reach a peak at about 200km and then decreases. The possible mechanism is also presented.

articleTitle: A Differential UWB Quasi-Yagi Antenna with a Notched Band at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact differential ultra-wide band (UWB) planar quasi-Yagi antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna can not only realize a wide differential-mode (DM) impedance bandwidth covering from 3.8 to 9.5 GHz, but achieve a high and wideband common-mode (CM) suppression by employing the balanced stepped-impedance microstrip-slotline transition structure. Besides, the DM passband is independent from the CM response, simplifying the design procedure significantly. In addition, a sharp DM notched band at 5.8 GHz is generated by adding one pair of quarter-wavelength short-circuited stubs adjacent to the microstrip line symmetrically. In order to illustrate the effectiveness of the design, one prototype of the antenna is designed, fabricated, and measured. A good agreement between the simulated and measured results is observed.

articleTitle: A New Type of Small Size and Multiband Antenna For Interphone Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a multiband, small size interphone antenna is designed. The antenna is structured by dielectric substrate, reference ground and radiating element. It is excited by a coaxial line with 50Ω characteristic impedance, and the operating frequencies include GSM850/900, DCS1800, PCS1900, GPS1575, UMTS2100, WLAN2400 and LTE2300/2500. The simulated results show that the S11 of antenna is less than -10dB in all of the bands except GSM850/900. The antenna has some advantages, easy for making and integrating, small size and low cost. So it can be used in interphone communication successfully.

articleTitle: Mixing Music Using Electromagnetic Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Acoustic reverberation chamber (RC) is a good facility to create reverb effect in music mixing. This paper presents the use of an electromagnetic (EM) RC to generate acoustic reverb effects. Different to an acoustic RC, stirrers are often used in an EM RC. Thus, it is easy to generate many chamber transfer functions with similar statistical characteristics; also the measured chamber transfer function can be post-processed to realize a complex reverb environment. Measurements are performed to demonstrate the results.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Circulary Polarized Ring-Slot Antenna with Shorted Section in the Ground
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band circularly polarized ring-slot antenna with shorted section in the ground. The dual-band is achieved using a single-layer microstrip-fed configuration coupled to two nested ring-slots. The circularly polarization is obtained by the asymmetric slot-ring. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna has well circularly polarization characteristics for left-hand circularly polarization (LHCP) in the lower-band and upper-band. The 10dB return loss impedance bandwidths for the lower-band and upper-band are 50.2% and 13.2% respectively. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 17%0 and 9.3% for the lower and upper band respectively.

articleTitle: Comparison of the air-sea flux algorithm for the evaporation duct diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Combing for the domestic and international diagnosis model of evaporation duct, the discrepancy of the parameter scheme of the flux algorithm in marine surface boundary layer is analyzed. The six parameter schemes of two roughness length functions (Fairall (2003), Liu (1979)) and three universal functions (LKB, RSHMU, Coare3.0) are compared using sea trial data. Show as a result: The accuracy of model decreases in shore with the increase of the stability, and is lower than open sea area. Under the different environment of sea area, the optimization combination (Fairall(2003) & Coare3.0) is confirmed.

articleTitle: A tunable filter based on dumbbell metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, based on the metamaterial principle of phase compensation, the broadband and high integration filter is designed. And by using the varactor diode loading technology to change the electromagnetic parameters (relative permittivity and relative permeability), the filter can be tunable in frequency. A dumbbell shaped slot metamaterial filter is designed in this paper. The measured results show that: the filter can be continuously tunable in the X band by loading varactor diode on the unit structure. when the varactor diode increases from 0.1pF to 0.7pF, the center frequency of the filter is decreased from 11.0GHz to 9.1GHz, the bandwidth is 25% (8.7GHz-11.2GHz), and the return loss minimum is 17dB, the insertion loss maximum is 1.2dB.

articleTitle: An array antenna calibration method based on GNSS signal
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An array antenna calibration method using satellite navigation signal is proposed. Through tracking satellite navigation signals received by different antenna elements, the amplitude and phase calibration parameters can be derived from signal power and carrier phase which are extracted from signal tracking loop. Simulation results show that using the calibration results based on GNSS signal in beamforming can get C/N0 gain almost the same as calculated from theory. The calibration method is simple and fast, thus can be easily embedded in GNSS receivers using array antenna.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of SKA Dish Prototype
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a brief review of the SKA dish prototype (SKA-P) included the optical and structural design is presented, and its structural and electrical performance is analyzed and measured. The results satisfy the SKA requirements.

articleTitle: Compact multi-channel terahertz wave demultiplexer
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate a compact multichannel terahertz demultiplexer which is composed of three photonic crystal directional couplers. By using plane wave expansion, the transmittance of the designed photonic crystal directional couplers are analyzed. Then, the performance of the demultiplexer based on the photonic crystal directional couplers is investigated with the aid of finite-difference time-domain method. The transmittances at frequencies of 0.57THz, 0.52THz, 0.54THz, and 0.6THz are 98%, 92%, 94%, and 88.2%, respectively. We confirm that the device can split four different terahertz wave frequencies into different output ports with high transmittance efficiency. In addition, the total size of the our terahertz demultiplexer is about 5.2mm×5.6mm, which can be easily integrated in terahertz circuit systems. This advice provides a new method to manipulate terahertz wave.

articleTitle: Joint Power and Position Estimation for the Blind Signal using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Utilizing the received power on the spatially distributed sensors can efficaciously infer the various characteristics of the active wireless transmitter. In this paper, the joint estimation problem of the transmit power and positions of one and multiple wireless nodes were studied, which was based on the received power by the sensors without any priori knowledge of its transmit power. A particle swarm optimization algorithm was proposed to estimate the transmitter locations and power. Such a method can achieve an original estimation without sufficient measurements from sensors. The particles were generated in the constrained testing area. And a signal initial position estimation algorithm was improved in this paper. The performance was verified throuzh numerical simulations.

articleTitle: The statistic characteristics of HF Oblique Sounding Channel at mid and low latitude during ionospheric disturbance time
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, historical data MOFF from two HF propagation paths: Qingdao-Lanzhou and Guangzhou-Haikou at mid and low latitude, the midpoint referenced data are from two ionosondes located at Xinxiang and Guangzhou, respectively. They are used to study the disturbance dMOFF properties reflected by the ionosphere during the ionospheric disturbance period, and compared with the variation of dMUF calculated by ITU-R P.533. The relative variation dfoF2 in the midpoint is used an indicator to denote the ionospheric disturbance magnitude. It is found that the change trends of dMOFF, dfoF2 and dMUF are similar to each other during the ionospheric disturbance time.

articleTitle: The LFM fuze Doppler extraction method based on band-pass sampling
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The linear FM Doppler fuze extract Doppler using secondary mixing method, which need more analog circuits and lead difficult to parameter adjustment. Direct IF sampling need higher sampling rate resulting in a large amount of data processing. Aiming at the problem, the linear FM fuze Doppler extraction method based on band-pass sampling is proposed in this paper. The method used band-pass sampling extract Doppler of linear FM Doppler fuze directly, not need secondary mixing and need subsequent analog circuits. The method not only extracts Doppler of linear FM Doppler fuze direct but also reduces the sampling rate. Simulation analysis and actual verification showed that the linear FM fuze Doppler extraction method based on band-pass sampling could extract Doppler, do not need secondary mixing and subsequent analog circuits, the amount of data after sampling is small and amount of data to be processed is small to.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Precision Array Laser Fuze Detection Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An optimization of lattice laser fuze simulation method based on ray tracing and scattering theory is proposed to eliminate the error resulted from the target simplification that could meet the requirement of the lattice laser fuze design and simulation. The ray tracing illumination model of computer graphics to describe the laser transmission process was optimized by combining the bidirectional reflection distribution function (BRDF) of the planar material with the ray tracing algorithm, in order to calculate the multiple scattering of the three-dimensional target laser to realize the simulation of the fuze echo signal. The simulation results showed that the model error was less than 20%, which could be used for the design and simulation of dot matrix ground detection laser fuze.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for LFM-Coding Radar Signals Classification
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Considering that classification of Linear Frequency Modulation-coding(LFM-coding) signals performs bad in complex electromagnetic environment, a methodology based on time-frequency fractal feature analysis and spatial data mining is presented. The method calculates the ambiguity function (AF) of radar signals, and extracts the rotation angles and fractal dimensions of AF main ridges as the feature parameters used to build feature vectors. Then on the basis of spatial data mining, nuclear field is employed to dig out the distribution characteristics of parameter samples in feature space and all samples are dynamically classified to different clusters under the guidance of field strength. Thus, the classification of LFM-coding signals is accomplished. Simulation results indicate that the extracted feature parameters have good stability and separability, and the average correct classification rate of LFM-coding signals can exceed 90% significantly in case of low SNR. The proposed method is proved to be effective when classifying LFM-coding radar signals in complex electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Asynchronous WCDMA Signal Long-Period Scrambling Code Estimation and Blind Decoding
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to estimate and decode the long-period scrambling code of asynchronous WCDMA signal, this paper proposed an independent component analysis (ICA) algorithm and phase locked loop (PLL) technology. First, according to the structure of WCDMA, the signal after sample rate conversion was proposed to be modeled as a form of carrier-modulated blind source separation matrix. Then, the long-period scrambling code and source information will be estimated by the proposed ICA and PLL algorithm. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively identify the long-period scrambling sequence of asynchronous multi-user WCDMA signals, and has better performance than the traditional identification method based on singular value decomposition(SVD).

articleTitle: Aspect Dependence of Parametric Instability Excitation by X-mode at EISCAT
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recent studies of X-mode wave heating experiments observed by EISCAT (European Incoherent Scatter Scientific Association) UHF radar indicate that parametric instability (PI) can be excited unexpectedly. In this paper, we re-investigate the ionospheric heating experiment on October 21, 2012 in details. The observed HF-enhanced ion lines (HFILs) and HF-enhanced plasma lines (HFPLs) observed during the experiment presents dependence on the heating incidence angles. The observational evidence and numerical calculation that the parallel electric field of X-mode heating wave can exceed the PI excitation threshold at certain angles indicate the decisive role of parallel electric field for the PI excitation. The excited HFPLs and HFILs during X-mode heating cycles also present the evidence for the non-Maxwellian distribution of the electrons in the heated region.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Protection Effect of the Short-wave RF Front-end Lightning Electromagnetic Pulse Protection Module Based on Switch-type and Voltage Limiting Type Protective Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces the basic structure and protection effect test result of the short-wave RF front-end lightning electromagnetic pulse protection module based on the switch-type protective element (gas discharge tube, GDT) and voltage limiting type protection element (transient voltage suppressor, TVS), and analyzes the reasons for the waveform difference during measurement of the residual output voltage of the module with a high-voltage probe and an attenuator respectively. The study herein shows that the action delay of the protection module under development is less than 1 ns and its leakage pulse peak is less than 50 V when the lightning electromagnetic pulse with a peak voltage of 10 kV, a rising rate of 10 kV/μs and a peak current of 5 kA is applied, and in addition, the high-voltage probe, when adopted to measure the residual output voltage waveform of the module, is sensitive to the external electromagnetic radiation field, which will produce an interference signal hard to be eliminated, with its amplitude and oscillation period in direct proportion to the area of the high-voltage probe test circuit; while the coaxial attenuator enjoys a higher measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: A Helix-loaded Equiangular Spiral Antenna with Compact Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband circular polarization antenna based on the composite structure of planar spiral and longitudinal helix is presented. Compared to single spiral antenna or helix antenna, proposed antenna has a better performance at low frequency by introducing two longitudinal helix arms connecting with the terminal of the planar spiral arms. As a result, the return loss, axial ratio (AR) and gain are both improved without increasing the antenna size. The antenna is designed to operate from 2 to 18 GHz and has a physical dimension of φ 50×45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A prototype was fabricated and tested, the results show that the proposed antenna can provide an AR of less than 2.5 dB, a return loss of less than -15 dB and a gain of greater than 0.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Programmable Metasurface for Manipulating Wi-Fi Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We, for the first time, present the programmable metasurface especially for the manipulation of the Wi-Fi signals with frequencies ranging from 2.402 to 2.483GHz in this work. This metasurface consists of an array of binary phase-coded meta units, which are electrically and independently controllable by changing the states of loaded PIN diodes. More specifically, for each meta unit, it has two phase states, and the phase difference of 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>±20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> when the state of its PIN diode is switched from ON (rep., OFF) to OFF(rep., on) at the desired wireless frequency band. Simulation of imaging examples and experimental results of meta units are provided to demonstrates its performance and important potential in manipulating arbitrarily Wi-Fi signals, which could fundamentally push forward information systems.

articleTitle: Reduced-order modeling methods of electromagnetic wave propagation in magnetized plasmas
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, reduced-order modeling methods of electromagnetic wave propagation in magnetized plasmas are considered. Firstly, the Current Density Convolution Finite Difference Time Domain (JEC-FDTD) method is used to obtain the true solution of the scattered electric field in parallel and perpendicular to the magnetic field in plasmas. Secondly, a low-order pattern library based on the dynamic behavior of control system is constructed by Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and machine learning. Finally, the model which is combined with compressive and POD library is verified by constructing the temporal-spatial electric fields with few samplings. The model will be of great significance for the invertion of plasma parameters and partial differential equations with sparse measurement data.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Ionospheric Stimulated Electromagnetic Emission Investigations (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Stimulated Electromagnetic Emission (SEE) is secondary radiation produced during experiments where high power high frequency (HF) radio waves interact with the ionosphere. SEE has been a vibrant area of investigation for the past three decades and SEE has been developed into an important remote sensing tool for the ionosphere with substantial potential for aeronomy studies. Past experiments primarily considered emissions within a bandwidth of 100 kHz of the pump (transmit) frequency, so-called wideband SEE (WSEE), but more recent work has concentrated on SEE within 1kHz of the pump frequency, so-called narrowband SEE (NSEE), as well as the pump frequency harmonic. A brief review of the recent experimental observations of NSEE are presented as well as some basic concepts of the nonlinear wave-wave processes that produce NSEE. Some new potential applications are discussed as well.

articleTitle: Individual Recognition of Communication Emitter Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the individual recognition problem of the communication emitter, this paper, starting with the subtle characteristics of the communication emitter in the signal layer, proposes a method of individual recognition based on deep learning. First, a recognition framework based on deep learning is established, and a convolution neural network containing two hidden layers is designed to extract local features through two layers convolution operations. Secondly, the stochastic gradient descent method is used to optimize the parameters, and the soft max model is used to determine the output label. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Clustering Analysis of Multipath Components in Urban Road Scenario for C-V2X Propagation Channels
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recently, the cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) communications have been widely investigated. The direct communication of terminals in the road environment is an important part of C-V2X. This paper focuses on the spatial distribution characteristics and clustering analysis of multipath components (MPCs) in the wireless channel when the terminal communicates directly. First, we obtain the MPCs based on measurement data, and use the K-means algorithm to cluster the MPCs. Then, according to the data processing results, the spatial characteristics of MPCs in urban roads scenario are analyzed. The results are useful for C-V2X channel modeling and communication system design.

articleTitle: Radiation Fields across Sea-air Interface from Underwater Magnetic Dipole Source
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to precisely calculating the fields in air from an underwater magnetic dipole source, a novel method to introduce a low-frequency source is proposed. This method is built up by combining the analytical solution of the magnetic dipole source in the conductive medium with the total-field scattered-field boundary condition. Numerical results verified the validity and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The Eeffects of Anode Foil Transmission Ratio on the Performance of Vircator
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Virtual cathode oscillator (Vircator) is an important high power microwave (HPM) source because of its simple structure and no magnetic field is required to maintain its operation. Cathode and anode are the two most important components in vircator. The anode transmission ratio decides the electron number that can cross over to the other side to form vircator oscillation and reflects the late electrons which also contribute to HPM output. In this article we investigate the effects of anode transmission ratio in a X-band vircator with three particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of 30%, 50%, and 70% anode transmission ratio, and found higher anode transmission ratio leads higher HPM output, less anode collision power loss, and slightly higher drift tube collision power loss, but high anode transmission ratio grid or foil are more difficult to manufacture.

articleTitle: Urban Macrocellular Field Strength Prediction for 230 MHz Electric Wireless Private Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the field strength is predicted for urban macrocellular TD-LTE 230MHz electric wireless private networks by using Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD). The total path loss including only diffraction, and diffraction plus reflection with respect to the transceiver heights and the number of buildings are calculated and analyzed by comparison with COST231 model, respectively. The results show that UTD model can simulate the path loss more accurately by considering the influence of buildings between the transceiver. The results in this paper are helpful for the coverage prediction of TD-LTE 230MHz electric wireless private networks.

articleTitle: Fast Antenna Design Using Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at reducing the large computation cost of traditional EM-driven antenna design methods, surrogate models based on back propagation neural networks (BPNN) are studied. In order to solve the problem of easily falling into local optimum in BPNN, a PSO-BPNN surrogate model is developed by improving initial structural parameters of neural networks and applied to fast multi-objective optimization design of multi-parameter antenna structures. Design results show that the proposed PSO-BPNN surrogate model can be integrating into multi-objective evolutionary algorithms for dealing with complex antenna designs with high-dimensional parameter space.

articleTitle: A New Broadband Circularly Polarized Monopole Antenna With Modified Ground
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This letter presents a new broadband circularly polarized (CP) monopole antenna with modified ground. The proposed antenna fed by coaxial probe consists of a square ground loaded with an L-shaped branch, which is capable of generating broadband CP radiation. In addition, an I-shaped slit is embedded into the ground plane to improve the impedance matching. The presented antenna has a 10 dB return loss bandwidth from 1.82 to 4.21 GHz (79.3% centered at 3.02 GHz), and a wide 3 dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth from 1.84 to 3.95 GHz (72.9% centered at 2.89 GHz). The measured gains are greater than 2.0 dBic in the AR band, and the gain variation within the AR band is less than 1 dBic, which means a good flat gain feature in the broad frequency band. Both the simulated and measured results validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Multi-functional Antenna with UHF and CP Performance for Communication and Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-functional antenna system for both communications and navigation is presented. The proposed antenna combined a sleeve monopole antenna for vertical polarization (VP) and a patch antenna for right-hand circular polarization (RHCP). The VP sleeve monopole element is designed for UHF band, and a spiral slot is etched around the side wall to reduce the height of the antenna. The RHCP element is an annular-ring patch antenna designed for Beidou B3 frequency band. The CP performance is realized by a small surface-mounted 0°-90° hybrid chip integrated in the feed network. The UHF antenna is co-located concentrically on the top of the patch antenna with a relative height of 0.03). An insulating gasket is put between the UHF and the B3 antenna for the compact structure. The UHF antenna achieves a bandwidth of 2% from 390 to 398 MHz and gain up to 2.7 dBi in the frequency band. The patch antenna works in a broad bandwidth covering the whole B3 band for RHCP. An port isolation of 25 dB is achieved in B3 band. Details of the antenna design as well as the simulated results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A Dual Circular Polarized Conical Conformal Sinuous Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A conformal sinuous antenna on 2.5-6.5GHz is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of four sinuous metal arms and two tapered microstrip baluns. The four arms are printed on a conical dielectric substrate by Laser Direct Structuring (LDS) technology. The VSWR of the antenna is less than 2.5:1 over the frequency band and the axial ratio (AR) of both left-hand and right-hand circular polarization are below 3dB.

articleTitle: Study on the absorption properties of two kinds of dihedral corner metamaterial absorbers
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The absorption properties of two different kinds of metamaterial structures which loaded over the dihedral corners are investigated under the incident microwaves of both TM and TE polarizations. Simulation results show that the dihedral corner metamaterial absorber (DCMA) can excite more absorption peaks than traditional planar metamaterial absorber (PMA) which have the same parameters of the unit cells. The DCMA is found to be polarization sensitive so it might be used as frequency selective absorber. Two different opening angles of the DCMA with these two structures are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Downlink Channel Estimation Based on Parametric Model in Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper investigates downlink channel estimation in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To reduce the overhead of downlink channel estimation and uplink feedback in FDD systems, cascaded precoding has been used in massive MIMO such that only a low-dimensional effective channel needs to be estimated and fed back. In this paper, we analyze a strategy for downlink channel estimation based on the parametric model in massive MIMO with cascaded precoding. The path delays of uplink channels are first estimated and quantized at the base station, then fed forward to the user equipment (UE) through a dedicated feedforward link. In this manner, the UE can obtain the a priori knowledge of the downlink channel in advance since it has been demonstrated that the downlink and the uplink channels can have identical path delays. Our analysis and simulation results show that the proposed approach can achieve near-MMSE performance.

articleTitle: Target Scattering Characteristics under Beam Illumination Based on MoM
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the case of antenna beam illumination, the RCS of the target at different distances from the antenna is calculated by the method of moments. And the calculation results are used to compare with the RCS under plane wave conditions. By analysing the trend of RCS, it is found under what conditions, the plane wave can be approximated as the calculation source. The scattering characteristics of the target in the case of local illumination are also considered. By comparing RCS with different size targets, it is found that the RCS of the partial target can be calculated to approximate the overall target. This conclusion can be used to simplify the calculation of the RCS of the electric large size target.

articleTitle: Design of Antenna Rapid Optimization Platform Based on Intelligent Algorithms and Surrogate Models
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Optimizers in electromagnetic (EM) simulation software are facing challenges in optimization efficiency, supported optimization types and optimization results usability. Aiming to fill these gaps, a new antenna design exploration scheme is proposed, called Antenna Rapid Optimization Platform (AROP). The scheme adopts ANSOFT HFSS and MATLAB co-simulation method and provides a friendly graphical interface based on the antenna optimization process. State-of-the-art intelligent optimization algorithms and surrogate model methods are embedded, addressing efficient multi-objective antenna optimization problems and generating Pareto optimal solution sets. Design results show that the surrogate models assisted by evolutionary algorithms built into AROP can largely improve optimization capacity for high-performance antenna synthesis and deal with complex antenna designs with high-dimensional parameter space.

articleTitle: Space target scattering characteristic imaging in the visible range based on ray tracing algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper simulated and calculated the visible light scattering of satellite target based on the material's bidirectional reflection distribution function (BRDF) and the reverse ray tracing algorithm, and on this basis, the target visible light imaging simulation is realized. The solar radiation in the visible range is calculated using the Modtran atmospheric transmission model. The ray tracing algorithm combined the geometric modeling of the target to realize occlusion and blanking judgment, and calculates the spatial distribution of target scattering intensity when visible light is incident.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband and Wide-angle Scanning Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband and wide-angle scanning tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) is presented in this paper. The simulation results show that the operating frequency range of the array is from 3.5GHz to 10.5GHz with the VSWR less than 3:1, while scanning up to 60° in E-plane and H-plane.

articleTitle: Investigations of Ionospheric E-region Field-aligned Irregularities Observed with Kunming VHF Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The statistical characteristics of mid-low latitude ionospheric E-region field-aligned irregularities (FAI) observed with the Kunming very high-frequency (VHF) radar are presented. First, the observational results show that the irregularities appeared mainly in periods before noon and near night, with the nighttime echoes being more intense and covering a greater height extent than that during the daytime. Second, we observed the existence of two well-defined types of echoes in the nighttime: the lower E-region echoes (115-130km) and upper E-region echoes (130-150km). Moreover, there are differences in FAI's motion characteristics at different range in the daytime and nighttime. Without in-field measurements, it is difficult to verify what physical mechanisms may explain the formation of the irregularities, which we will combine other facilities to analyze it in the future.

articleTitle: A novel compact microstrip dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) using embeded SIRs for WLAN/WiMax application
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel compact microstrip dual-band bandpass filter using embedded SIRs for WLAN/WiMax application is presented in this letter. The filter consists of a main resonator and two embedded resonators. The first passband is generated by main resonator, the second one is created by the embedded resonators. Detail operating principle of the filter is described in this study. Furthermore, the overall circuit size is very compact with only 21 mm×9 mm due to the embedded configuration. A proposed dual-band filter has been fabricated and testing, and the measured results agree well with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: C-Band ISAR Imaging for the Precision Expandable Radar Calibration Sphere
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Precision Expandable Radar Calibration Sphere (PERCS) is newly designed for high frequency (HF) radar calibration satellite. There is potential for the PERCS to operate for the C-Band radar calibration. The wire frame structure has several advantages over traditional calibration satellites. This paper aims to realize the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging for PERCS at C-Band. The bidirectional analytic ray tracing (BART) method is employed to fast calculate the backscattering fields from PERCS. Two-dimensional ISAR imaging of the V180 model are simulated for full polarizations. The imaging results agree with the geometrical structure of the sphere, which may be promising in radar calibration satellite design.

articleTitle: A Multiple Bands Absorber Based on Curved Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We numerically investigate the absorption property of a type of curved metamaterial absorber (CMA) in the microwave regime. Simulation results demonstrate that the CMA can perform absorption peaks at four resonant frequencies correspond to the fundamental, the second order, the third order and the forth order resonance frequencies respectively. This simple absorber is desirable for potential applications in improving absorbance performances.

articleTitle: A Dual Circularly Polarized Rectenna with Wide-Beam
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-circularly polarized rectenna, with a wide 3-dB axial-ratio beam-width, operating in the WIFI band(the central frequency is 2.4GHz) is proposed for harvesting the ambient radio frequency (RF) energy. Here, the rectenna with two 50-Ω microstrip-fed ports are designed to realize both right-hand and left-hand circular polarization. Good isolation is achieved by reasonably adjusting the radius of the annular slots and the length of the feed microstrip. A prototype is manufactured and tested. Measured results are in reasonably good agreement with the simulated ones, exhibiting a 3-dB AR beam-width as wide as 120° for both LHCP and RHCP. The measured polarization isolation is better than 20dB at 2.4GHz and reflection coefficient is better than 15 dB within the working band. In addition, the 3-dB ARBW is approximately 6.25% (2.32-2.48 GHz).

articleTitle: Study on Factors Influencing the Ionospheric Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric conductivity is an important parameter to describe the state of the ionosphere. There is a certain distribution law of the conductivity with the change of solar local time, latitudes and altitudes. In addition, some physical factors have direct effects on ionospheric conductivities. How these elements, such as solar activities, the geomagnetic index, electron temperature and electron density, influence it has been studied in this thesis, which will provide theoretical foundations and ideas for changing ionospheric conductivities manually.

articleTitle: CPML Implementation for FCC-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The convolutional perfectly matched layer is implemented for the face-centered cubic grid which can substitute the standard Cartesian (Yee) grid. The face-centered cubic grid proves to have better grid isotropy and relaxed stability criterion. Here, we implemented the convolutional perfectly matched layer as an absorbing boundary for the face-centered cubic computational domain. The efficiency of the convolutional perfectly matched layer is demonstrated by comparing the reflection error obtained in face centered cubic grid with the reflection error in the Yee's grid.

articleTitle: Wideband Channel Measurement Over the Horizon
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Spread spectrum sliding correlation method is used for wide channel measurement at non-line-of-sight over sea in this paper. Time domain channel measurement is a common method in remote measurement which can obtain channel impulse response(CIR) directly. Through this method we calculated delay spread of the multipath over-the-horizon at sea.

articleTitle: A Method of Retrieving Tropospheric Refractivity Above Ocean Surface using GNSS
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed a method of retrieving tropospheric refractivity above ocean surface using Global Navigation Satellite System, which takes the Final Analysis Data of Global Forecast System as background data, and uses intelligent optimization algorithm to train the inversion-network. the method can get tropospheric refractivity profile in any sea area after the zenith tropospheric delay and the atmospheric temperature, humidity, pressure were measured, and it can be used in refraction error correction applications such as radar detection and space tracking. It has less cost than radiosonde but higher precision than traditional empirical model. In addition, it can be used in real time and has higher temporal and spatial resolution.

articleTitle: A study of tropospheric scattering model based on coherent source-induced atmospheric refractivity fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The physical mechanism of generating the lasting tropospheric refractivity fluctuation with stable array-distributed structure by coherent acoustic waves is investigated. Based on the array antenna principle, a more accurate refractive index fluctuation model considering the phase shift effect of the sound source array is established, and structure of the artificial dielectric irregularities is simulated and analyzed. The refractive index distribution of tropospheric scatter communication links is found to be stratified, which lays a foundation for the calculation of tropospheric scattering.

articleTitle: Design of an S-Band Equilateral Triangular Patch Antenna (ETPA) on Mushroom Metamaterials in Compact Configuration
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An equilateral triangular patch antenna (ETPA) in compact configuration is designed operating in the S-band. The compacting effect is realized by loading triangular mushroom metamaterial structures in a low index natural substrate. The ETPA is demonstrated in ANSYS HFSS. Simulated results show that the side length of the ETPA is 0.27λ0. The -10dB bandwidth is 1.5%. The gain performance is acceptably high that the simulated result is 6.4dBi. These results prove that the compact ETPA can be used for future wireless applications.

articleTitle: Development of a Spherical Vacuum Window for Cryogenic Receiver
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Vacuum window is a key part of a cryogenic receiver, which isolate the feed from the ambient environment. Traditional flat vacuum window leads to a metal flange over the aperture of the feed, which inevitably distorts the radiation pattern of the feed and degrades the performance of the reflector antenna. This paper presents a spherical vacuum window made of Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA), which minimizes the negative effects on performance. And the measured results matches reasonably well with the simulation.

articleTitle: Study on the Propagation Characteristics of Indoor Millimeter-wave at 37.2GHz by SBR Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: At present, the effective method for studying the characteristics of indoor millimeter-wave propagation is the SBR method. In this paper, received power and delay spread for indoor line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight propagation are studied by SBR method. The correctness of the results is verified by comparison with relevant measurement data.

articleTitle: Bi-iterative MVDR Beamforming based on Beamspace Preprocessing for MIMO radars
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a bi-iterative minimum-variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming technique based on the beamspace preprocessing is proposed to solve two typical problems of the traditional MVDR beamformers in multi-input multi-output (MIMO) radars. Firstly, the omnidirectional power is radiated by traditional MIMO radars, however, the interested target is usually located in a certain spatial area. The unnecessary radiation on other areas will reduce the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of the MVDR beamformer. To solve this problem, a transmit beamspace preprocessing by second order cone programming (SOCP) is utilized to focus the energy in the interested region. Secondly, the MVDR beamformer in MIMO radars usually requires a great number of training samples and very high computation load, since both the transmitted degrees of freedom (DoF) and the received DoF are fully utilized. To tackle with these problems, a bi-iterative MVDR beamforming algorithm is proposed based on the beamspace preprocessing. Simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed beamforming algorithm.

articleTitle: SAL imaging method based on Kirchhoff approximation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Synthenic aperture lidar (SAL) has been widely used for Its high-precision image of remote targets. In order to study the influence of different shapes and different roughness targets on SAL image in Thz band, the SAL images of different with different roughness are numerically simulated in this paper. Rough surface is generated by monte-calro method, and rough object modeling by rough surface. By using Kirchhoff approximation (KA) the back-scattering filed of a rough object is obtained, and the SAL image of a rough object is obtained by the backscattering filed at different azimuth angles and frequencies. In this paper, the SAL image of simple plate target, circular and complex target are simulated, the result of SAL image show that the image can reflect not only the shape of the target but also the roughness of the target, it is specifically analyzed in this paper. During the imaging, different frequency-domain width, frequency-domin sampling accuracy and angular sampling accuracy will affect the SAL image. The wider frequency-domin width, the higher the accuracy, the better the imaging result, but only need to meet the requirements within a reasonable range, this paper analyzed that.

articleTitle: Compact Directional Coupler for High-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and miniaturized coupler is designed for high-power applications with coupling of about - 53dB in the frequency band between 10 ~ 100 MHz. The coupler is composed of a compact coaxial line and a series of equalizers. Such design exhibits high power handling capacity (up to 2 kW), flat coupling of -53 dB, and high directivity (more than 30 dB). And the coupling value can also be conveniently tuned by the equalizers.

articleTitle: High Power Metamaterial Based Dielectric Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A cross-shaped dielectric reflectarray element with continuous variation of permittivity is proposed in this paper. An improved method is used to retrieve the effective permittivity of a slab of metamaterial from its S parameters. A continuously changed permittivity from 1.4 to 5.0 and a full 360° range of phase shifts is successfully achieved at 9.3GHz from the simulation results. The power capacity of the element could reach 371Kw to accommodate to high power situations. A reflectarray of 20×20 elements is modeled and simulated to verify the radiation properties. Simulation results show that the main beam direction of 25° and the maximum gain of 25.4 dB are realized as expected. The new Fused Deposition Modeling(FDM) 3D printing approach can be deployed for the antenna fabrication with significantly reduced labor time and material costs.

articleTitle: Beam-Switching Lens Antenna at 26GHz for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A 26GHz lens antenna for 5G communications is presented in this paper. It consists of a specially designed dielectric lens and a feed, which is made of five linear subarrays with two microstrip patches per subarray (10 elements in total) etched on a 0.5-mm-thick substrate. A prototype has been designed and manufactured. The proposed antenna is capable of beam steering and achieving high gain with a light polyamide lens. The simulation and measured results on return loss and radiation characteristics are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Effects of Ionospheric Multi-path on Echo Spectra in HF Hybrid Sky-surface Wave System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In high-frequency (HF) hybrid sky-surface wave system, owing to the ionosphere propagation mode, the echo spectrum of hybrid sky-surface wave propagation channel are extremely complex in spatial, time, and frequency domains, which seriously affect radar performance. Using the newly-developed hybrid sky-surface wave experimental system and the oblique incidence sounders (OIS), the echo spectra for hybrid sky-surface wave propagation channel and the ionospheric propagation paths are obtained separately. The typical examples of echo spectra via the different propagation paths are analyzed. For ionospheric one-path propagation, the Range-Doppler spectra include sea clutter and ionospheric direct wave via one mode, which is conductive for target detection and location. For ionospheric multi-path propagation, the echoes via multi-path interact with each other, and the qualities of spectra reduce, which would seriously affect ship target detection. It is found that the propagation mode of echo spectra vary complicatedly with frequency and ionosphere state. This research could provide important supporting functions for operating frequency selection, target detection, and location.

articleTitle: Broadband Wide Beam Dual Polarization Antenna Unit and Its Sparse Array
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of wide-bandwidth beam antenna, which uses a relatively new type of cross-type microstrip dipole. This form has a wider -3dB beamwidth than ordinary microstrip antennas. The radiation profile uses a gradation profile and widens the bandwidth of the antenna by adding parasitic structures and increasing the air frame height. Antenna structure parameters are optimized using ANSYS HFSS. What the test results display is that the 1 port and 2 port standing wave's relative bandwidth <;-7.5dB of designed antenna unit reach 35.9% and 22.8%, the central frequency E-plane and H-plane beam width are 110 ° and 91 °, respectively, which facilitates large-angle scanning. This antenna is an orthogonal two-line polarized antenna with a zenith-directional line polarization cross-polarization level of -19.55 dB. With the help of software Matlab, we use sparse Focuss algorithm obtain the antenna array composed of 64 units. The gain reaches 19.61dB when the scanning angle is 60°. It was verified that this antenna element and sparse array have good characteristics.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Broadband Resonant Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a dual-polarized broadband Resonant Cavity Antenna (RCA), which is composed of a superstrate and a feed antenna. The superstrate is double-deck structure, where the superstratum is composed of circular patch cells and substratum is composed of circular aperture cells. This shows positive reflection coefficient phase, which in turn helps in obtaining wider RCA half-power fractional bandwidth. The feed system is a dual-polarized broadband aperture coupled patch antenna, which is composed of square resonant patch and dual-layer feed network. In order to feed energy to resonant patch, cross-shaped slot was cut away from the ground. Simulated results show that this RCA owns 2GHz (9GHz-I1GHz) S11=-10dB impedance bandwidth where the RCA can obtain 13.33dBi-14.17dBi gain. Additional results will be presented during the symposium.

articleTitle: Transition Point of the Radio Wave Propagation Generated by Antennas in Rectangular Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radio wave propagation characteristics generated by antennas in rectangular tunnels are studied in this paper. A hybrid propagation model is used to describe the propagation characteristics, and the property of the transition points between different propagation models (regions) are analyzed by the waveguide modal method. The results indicate that the location of the transition point is significantly related to the beam width and beam direction of the transmitting antenna and the tunnel dimension. The results are valuable for layout design of the antenna system of wireless communication in confined space.

articleTitle: An Efficient Parallelization Approach of FEM-DDM for Large-Scale 3D Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We present in this paper an efficient parallelization approach of the finite element domain decomposition method (FEM-DDM) for large scale 3D scattering problems. In this parallel FEM-DDM, the domain decomposition is done in a hierarchical way to minimize the inter-processor communication. In the hierarchical domain decomposition scheme, the whole FEM solution domain is first decomposed into large size subdomains with a total number equals to MPI processes. Then, each large subdomain is distributed to a MPI process and further decomposed into smaller ones to achieve good computation efficiency. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, scalability, and capability of the proposed parallel FEM-DDM algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimization Analysis of Non-Uniform Array Antennas for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The non-uniformly spaced sparse array antenna can save a lot of cost, and adopts the method that the antenna array element is thinned on a certain aperture to realize the array design, and can obtain higher gain through fewer antenna array elements, thereby achieving higher resolution which in turn simplifies the structure and reduces the cost, has therefore become a hot topic of research. This paper proposed genetic algorithm to analyze the optimization characteristics of uniform and non-uniformly spaced sparse array antennas for millimeter wave.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Extraction for Coaxial-to-Microstrip Transition Structure Using Response Surface Method
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Coaxial-to-microstrip transition structure is a common discontinuity structure in the assembly processing of microwave electronic products. A simple and accurate equivalent circuit extraction method of coaxial-to-microstrip discontinuous structure is proposed in this paper. Response surface methodology (RSM) is applied to the extraction of the equivalent circuit of the coaxial-to-microstrip discontinuous structure for the first time. The equivalent circuit is obtained at a wide frequency band 5-40 GHz, and the explicit formulas of the model element for the equivalent circuit are given. The equivalent circuit can be embedded in the existing circuit analysis simulation software, which can greatly decrease the simulation time and have great potential for the real applications.

articleTitle: Multiple Combinational Algorithm to Adaptively Track and Detect Measurement While Drilling Electromagnetic Wave Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Band-pass filter is frequently used in measurement while drilling (MWD) system of electromagnetic (EM) wave transmission, so as to remove out-of-band noise. However, such design will increase the error rate of decoding when dealing with non-stationary time varying signal and especially in-band signal. By studying features of EM-MWD transmission and channel noise jamming, a multiple combinational algorithm that can adaptively track and detect EM signal is proposed in this article. This algorithm is a combination of low-pass filtering, five-point triple smoothing, adaptive notch, adaptive cancellation and line enhancement, and it takes recursive least squares as its principle of adaptive tracking. As theoretical analysis and simulation show, such algorithm can effectively extract useful signal from noise-contaminated signal and reduce the bit error rate, which lays a good foundation for further decoding.

articleTitle: Capacity of Massive MIMO System Based on Indoor Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison of antenna correlation between a uniform linear array (ULA) and a uniform circular array (UCA) topological Massive MIMO (Multiple-input multiple-output) system is presented. We conduct a measurement campaign at a building hall scenario with bandwidth of 100MHz at 6GHz and extract the spatial correlation parameter. It is shown that antenna elements are deeply correlated and the envelope correlation coefficients show negative exponential down-trend with the increasing of antenna spacing in Massive MIMO systems. Furthermore, we investigate the system capacity. And then impact of spatial correlation on capacity is graphically presented, which is compared with simulation results of Rayleigh independent and identically distributed channel. Measurement campaign verifies the antenna correlation real exists, which decreased the system capacity.

articleTitle: The Method of Adaptive Gaussian Decomposition Based Recognition and Extraction of Scattering Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the methods of Near-Field ISAR imaging based Near-Field Far-Field Transformation (NFFFT), all target scattering is assumed to occur at the location of the incident field excitation. It's obviously non-localized scattering phenomenon such as re-entrant cavity scattering and surface traveling waves cannot be effectively handled. The presented method could find out where the non-localized scattering phenomenon occurred and separate from the scattering signatures. Then we can emendate the non-localized scattering part and improve the NFFFT precision. We present a method for recognition and extraction of scattering mechanisms. Firstly, calculate the spectrogram of target's scattering echo by an adaptive time-frequency transformation method named Adaptive Gaussian Representation (AGR). Then separate the wide components and narrow components of the Gaussian functions from the echo. Making images by the two parts respectively, the local and non-local scattering mechanisms and where it happened can be recognized. Beside of the NFFFT using, the method we presented could also be used to recognize and extract scattering mechanisms in complex target, and can be used in stealth design, SAR/ISAR image processing, etc.

articleTitle: The Investigation of Compact Handheld Terminal MIMO Antenna for 4G/5G Application
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A hybrid 10×10 MIMO antenna covering seven-bands is proposed for 4G/5G applications, where the corresponding 4G (2-antenna array) and 5G (8-antenna array) antenna modules are respectively responsible for the GSM850/900/DCS1800/PCS1900/UMTS/LTE2300/2500 and C-band. In this design, for the 4G application, the short-circuiting belt and the matching circuit are employed to reduce the longitudinal dimension and broaden the bandwidth, and both the return loss (S11) and isolations (S21) are improved by using the hybrid method of combining the additional M-strip extended-ground with the neutralization line (NL) techniques. The simulated whose return loss, isolation and radiation patterns are all as predicted.

articleTitle: Fast-Shaping of Reflector Antenna Illuminated by Quasi-Actual Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A time-saving method to reshape the surface of reflector antenna fed by a quasi-actual feed(QAF) based on the Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline Surface (NURBS) technique, ray tracing technology (RT), physical optical method (PO), and Gauss-Legendre integral (GLI), is proposed. The optimized surface of the reflector can be smooth and time-saving by NURBS algorithm to support its better agreement with its future manufactured counterpart and by RT-PO-GLI method, where the antenna is fed by a QAF derived from the far-field data of an antenna model simulated from the commercial software MWS Studio CST, not a pure imaginary feed like in the available literature. An objective function is constructed with the weights of main-lobe level, side-lobe level, and beam width of the considered antenna to regulate the method to optimize electric far-field radiation patterns to specific purpose. The results show that the method has a faster calculating speed and can surely be expected to design a reshaped reflector antenna effectively and fast.

articleTitle: Optimize and design of coupling antenna for TM021 resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel technique for coupling enhancement of coaxial antenna fed TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</sub> resonant cavity is proposed in this paper. An inverted frustum section is inserted between the coaxial waveguide and the resonant cavity to improve coupling. The inverted frustum section acts as an impedance matching device that increases the coupling from waveguide to resonant cavity. The proposed structure has been simulated using Ansoft HFSS. The effect of various design parameters of the antenna on return loss characteristics is studied.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Band Ortho-Mode Transducer in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The OMT is designed to operate at two frequency bands, with each band passing an orthogonal polarization. For one polarization the band is 16.4-22 GHz and the other 24.4-31 GHz. In order to achieve the miniaturization of the structure, the paper adopts the following preferred techniques: loading two structurally symmetric coupling slots at the lateral ports to facilitate the elimination of high-order mode transmission; in addition, designing one of the coupling slots as a short-circuit structure for more effective reduction of the overall size and more conducive to processing. The high-frequency simulation software CST-2015 was used to optimize the design, and the best results were obtained: the overall length is only 24mm, the return loss is better than -20db in the working frequency band and the port isolation is better than -75dB.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Fiber Reinforced Composites with Random Fluctuation Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We propose a modified homogenization model by considering fiber reinforced composites with the random fluctuation microstructure in practical manufacturing craft. Several unknown factors are introduced in the proposed homogenization model to describe the behaviors of random fluctuation. Three infinite composite sheets are selected for validating the model. Unknown factors in this model can be obtained by using the least squares approximation easily. Then the results of shielding effectiveness (SE) obtained from proposed model are compared to numerical results from actual fiber reinforced composite structure in commercial software. Reasonable agreements indicate that the proposed model can efficiently estimate SE.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Radar Absorbing Structure Based on Lossy Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel design of a metamaterial absorber with wideband absorption, wide incident angle and polarization insensitivity. Based on resistive film structure (lossy frequency selective surface), this metamaterial absorber unit consists of a nut ring shaped resistance film, a polymethacrylimide foam and a metallic ground. Simulated reflectivity and absorption rate show that the absorber has a strong absorption of over 90% for normal incident wave. The absorption band ranges from 4.05GHz to 17.96GHz, basically covering C, X and Ku band. Simultaneously, the absorber has no significant change for TE or TM wave at different polarization angle, showing good polarization insensitivity. The absorber also exhibits broad angle absorption characteristics of over 80% absorption with incident angle from 0–40°. The reason for the wideband absorption characteristic of the absorber is quantitatively explained from the perspective of multi-reflection interference theory. The calculated results agree well with simulated ones.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Amplitude Equalizer Implemented in Feed Network of Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A miniaturized wideband amplitude equalizer is presented in this paper. The proposed equalizer is obtained by using LC series resonator and LC parallel resonator. For the demand of miniaturization and low-cost of the feed network of phased array antennas systems, the MMIC (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit) technology is used to implement the physical layout of the proposed amplitude equalizer. The EM simulation results indicate that the amplitude equalizer, with 3dB amplitude equalization capacity (positive slope) and a size of 0.8mm×0.54mm×0.1mm, can be applied in the feed network of phased array antennas.

articleTitle: Efficient Linear Array Synthesis Including Coupling Effects Utilizing Quantum Search Algorithm and Active Element Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel method incorporating the active element pattern (AEP) into the quantum search algorithm (QSA) procedure is presented to efficiently synthesize linear microstrip antenna arrays including mutual coupling. The proposed method has better pattern synthesis accuracy than the gravitational search algorithm (GSA). Numerical examples are given for synthesizing the Cosec-squared patterns of microstrip antenna arrays. Synthesis results show the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Stations Distribution to HF TDOA Geolocation Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The time difference of arrival (TDOA) geolocation technology in High Frequency (HF) propagation achieves accurate positioning due to various factors, including time difference measured by receiving stations, ionospheric parameters, and accurate propagation path mode et. The distribution of short-wave receiving stations is also an important factor affecting the geolocation accuracy. The problem of the stations distribution to the TDOA geolocation of HF propagation channel realized by Quasi-Parabolic (QP) ionospheric model is simulated. The results show that the geolocation result of the symmetrical distribution of the substations is better, and the main station falls on the mid-perpendicular line of the sub-stations.

articleTitle: Dosimetry Assessment for Human Exposure to Extremely Low Frequency Magnetic Fields in the Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, the magnetic flux density was measured in the rear seats of ten different electric vehicles. The measurement results were used to evaluate the induced electrical field in adult and infant models. The results demonstrated that the measured fields in the rear seats were far below the reference levels by the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection. The induced E-field strengths in infant were much lower than that of adults due to their smaller physical dimensions.

articleTitle: A Compact Combined Antenna for Pulse Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact combined antenna is proposed for pulse radiation in a UWB radar detection system in this paper. An exponentially tapered TEM horn is selected as the basic structure as well as the main radiated part, and a loading structure is used to improve its performance at low frequencies. Simulation results show that the loading structure generates a new radiator like a bow-tie antenna, decreasing the antenna size while not impacting the excellent radiating characteristics of the TEM horn antenna. The proposed structure has the advantages of wide bandwidth, compact size and high power capacity. As an antenna used for pulse radiation, the transmitted signal has little trailing and high EPP value in the time domain. Finally, the antenna is implemented and measured. The dimension of the antenna is 160mm*330mm* 110mm, and it can work from 250MHz to over 3GHz with the return loss below 7.5dB.

articleTitle: Wireless Coverage Analysis for Intra-Wagon Scenario at 60 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Very high throughput (VHT) intensive applications which demand a high data rate of Gigabits per second, motivate the exploration of millimeter-wave (mmWave) band, such as 60 GHz. With the new era of “smart rail mobility”, surfing the Internet, in general, accessing the network has become the fundamental part of the rail traffic services. Hence, this paper discusses the wireless coverage, which is the core of network planning, for intra-wagon scenario at 60 GHz band. First, the three-dimensional (3D) high-speed train (HST) model is reconstructed according to the actual size of China Railways CRH5. Then, we utilize a self-developed reliable ray-tracing (RT) simulator and set various parameters proposed by IEEE 802.11ad, which is a typical standard operating at 60 GHz band. Our result indicates that the wireless coverage is maximized while maximizing the number of the transmitters and the combination of transmit power and antenna gain. By considering the balance of the wireless coverage and the cost of the transmitters, the deployment of two transmitters in one wagon is suggested.

articleTitle: An Efficient Domain Decomposition Method Using Phase Extracted Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient overlapping domain decomposition method based on surface integral equations is presented for solving electromagnetic scattering from large-scale perfect electric conducting objects. In this method, the object is divided into a set of overlapping sub-domains, and the corresponding sub-domain problems are solved one by one so that the peak memory requirement for simulation can be significantly reduced. To further improve the efficiency of this method, the surface electric currents are expanded with the phased extracted basis functions defined over large curvilinear patches. Moreover, instead of introducing several layers of mesh cells as the buffer regions, this method only uses a single layer of jagged triangular mesh cells as the buffer regions, leading to a minimum number of extra unknowns in subdomain problems and a more convenient construction process for the buffer regions. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Comparison of ELF/VLF radiation excitation by different modes in EISCAT modulation heating experiment
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: By analyzing the experimental data of ionospheric modulation heating during EISCAT experiment, it is shown that the intensity of the ELF/VLF signal excited by AM mode is one order of magnitude higher than that of BW mode. However, compared with AM mode, the ELF/VLF excited by BW mode has no harmonic component, that is, the BW mode excitation ELF/VLF signal quality is better than the AM mode.

articleTitle: Paraxial Propagation of the Second-order Airy Vortex Beams in the Free Space
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper studies the propagation of the second-order Airy vortex beams in the free space. Based on the Huygens diffraction integral formula, the analytical expression for the propagation of a second-order Airy vortex beam is derived. We present the intensity and phase distributions of the second-order Airy vortex beams at different distances.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka Broadband Satellite Communication Antenna for Low-Earth-Orbit Constellation
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the demand of small-aperture portable terminals for low-earth-orbit satellite communication, a Ka-band petaloid splash-plate reflector antenna loaded with polystyrene is presented in this paper. Compared to the traditional reflector antennas, the proposed antenna has a wide working band, a high radiation efficiency and a low profile. The main reflecting surface of the proposed antenna adopts a design of split-disassembly structure, and the sub-reflecting surface requires no additional supporting rods, which makes the antenna smaller and more portable. The designed antenna can work at 17.7GHz to 20.2GHz for reception and 27.5GHz to 30.0GHz for transmission. The electrical performance of the antenna is simulated by considering the influence of the structural and processing design. The simulated results show that the VSWR of the antenna across the whole operating band is less than 2, and the aperture efficiency at the reception band and the transmission band is 57%~68% and 50%~62% respectively. The correctness of the simulated results were verified by different simulation algorithms, which provides a strong support for the subsequent engineering design.

articleTitle: Measurement of Scattering Coefficient in Time-Domain and Error Analysis of Dielectric Plate
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The key point and difficulty in measuring the electromagnetic properties of a medium is to accurately obtain its scattering coefficient. This paper proposes a specific scheme for measuring the scattering coefficient of dielectric plates based on ultra-wideband time domain measurement system. The acquisition and processing of experimental data are also analyzed in detail in the paper. To eliminate the measurement error caused by background and diffraction, method of “time window” and signal truncation are adopted in this paper. The measurement results of plate dielectric material in the frequency range of 2-26GHz show the reliability of this method is good, and has the advantages of fast access broadband reflection coefficient in a measurement.

articleTitle: Study on methods for suppression of Ionospheric Amplitude Contamination on OTHR
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Since the absorption and polarization caused by anisotropy, dispersion and time varying of the ionosphere, amplitude and phase contaminations exist in the echo signal of a sky-wave radar. The cause and distribution of the amplitude contamination is given in this paper. Furthermore, the effects of amplitude contamination on the echo of sky-wave radar are analyzed from time domain and space domain. Through simulation, the results show that amplitude contamination can cause main-lobe spread and side-lobe raising. Based on the above analysis, this paper puts forward an algorithm of restraining amplitude contamination. Simulation test demonstrates that the proposed algorithm is efficient.

articleTitle: A Miniature UWB Bandpass Filter Using Fractal Stepped Impedance Resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A ultra-wideband (UWB) and ultra compact bandpass filter constructed by connecting two short stubs on a stepped-impedance split ring resonator(SISRR) was developed. On the basis of the analysis of the feedback, the bandwidth of the lower and upper changes the short stub can be independently controlled, load, the design and optimization of the simplification of the procedures. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement in the full operating frequency band from 2.2 GHz to 10.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for PD Measurement Using the Equipment Shell Slot as Sensing Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
