abstract: Most of the existing high-voltage electrical equipment in operation uses external or internal Ultra High Frequency (UHF) detection sensors when detecting partial discharge (PD) signals, which brings difficulties to the already operating equipment. Based on the basic theory of slot antenna and the equipment shell itself, a novel method for PD detection is proposed in this paper: use the existing slots of the equipment shell as sensing antenna for PD measurement. In this paper, simulation models are built by the electromagnetic simulation software Ansoft HFSS to study the characteristics of shell slots as sensing antennas. The Laboratory simulations are also conducted. The research shows that the shell slot can be used as an antenna to receive the electromagnetic wave of PD inside the equipment and receive PD signals of different frequency ranges based on different sizes of the shell slot, which greatly reduces the difficulty of on-line PD detection. The conclusion of this study subverts the conventional design of UHF PD sensor and provides an important guiding direction and theoretical basis for improving the sensor design of UHF detection system.

articleTitle: A fast integration algorithm for detection of weak space debris using incoherent scatter radar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ever-increasing space debris circling over geospace can be hard to detect by use of ground-based radar due to its small size and high-order radial motion, which can easily lead to considerable integration loss. In this paper, we propose an efficient method that can achieve good integration performance for moving targets like space debris, of up to second-order dynamics, meaning only velocity and acceleration be taken into account. Overall, range migration can be resolved by limiting the integration number so that all echoes of different pulses are within the same range unit. As for doppler migration problem, we use the combination of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Inverse Fourier Transform (IFFT) to compute and compensate for velocity and acceleration terms, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of W-band Sub-harmonic Balanced Mixer Using $0.1\mu \mathrm{m}$ GaAs pHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a W-band (90GHz-110GHz) sub-harmonic single balanced mixer using a commercial 1.1μm GaAs pHEMT process from WIN Semi. Corp. Marchand balun at the LO port and matched filter circuit at the RF port and IF port are used to achieve excellent local oscillator (LO) to radio frequency (RF) and LO to intermediate frequency (IF) isolation. The proposed mixer operates with LO drive power 10 dBm and the conversion loss reaches 10 dB with a RF bandwidth more than 10 GHz. The achieved LO-to-IF isolation is better than 80 dB and the LO-to-RF and RF-to-IF isolation are better than 47 dB and 20 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Broadband Linear Polarization Converter and Its Application in RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 3-branch metasurface is proposed, acting as a linear polarization converter, which can efficiently convert linearly polarized electromagnetic waves to cross polarized waves within a wide frequency band. Based on the electric and magnetic resonant features of the unit cell, composed by 3-branch structure, three resonances are generated and lead to the bandwidth expansion of cross-polarization reflections. An average polarization conversion ratio of more than 90% from 11 GHz to 35GHz can be achieved. Furthermore, the designed metasurface exhibits its potential applications in monostatic and bistatic RCS reduction.

articleTitle: The Statistic and Analysis of Atmospheric Ducts Using ECMWF Global Analysis Fields
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric ducts have a significant impact on electromagnetic wave propagation. Studying the distribution feature of atmospheric ducts is of great significance for analyzing electromagnetic wave propagation. Calculate the feature value of atmospheric ducts using ERA-interime data, and these value are verified by rocketsonde data, On this basis, the global ducts probability is analyzed based on 6 years ERA-interime data in this paper. The conclusion is that the trade wind belt in the eastern part of the ocean and the western part of the continent is the high probability zone of the atmospheric ducts. There are six high probability zones (occurrence probability >50%) on the ocean, which are the North Pacific Ocean High Probability Zone, the South Pacific Ocean High Probability Zone, the North Atlantic Ocean High Probability Zone, the South Atlantic Ocean High Probability Zone, the North Indian Ocean High Probability Zone, and the South Indian Ocean Western Australia High Probability Zone; There are three little or no duct zones: Intertropical Convergence Zone, Mid-High Latitude Zone in the Northern Hemisphere, and Mid-High Latitude Zone in the Southern Hemisphere. The position, range, and probability of occurrence of these high and low probability zones of the atmospheric ducts have seasonal variations.

articleTitle: A terahertz frequency selective surface band-pass filter
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper describes a terahertz filter based on frequency selective surface with periodic Jerusalem cross slot cell. The filter is a two-stage band-pass filter fabricated with double-side Au film and the central frequency is 220GHz. The electromagnetic modeling, simulation and analysis of the bandpass filter are presented. The influence of the dimension of the Jerusalem cross cell on the transmission characteristics of the band-pass filter is discussed. By optimizing the dimension of the Jerusalem cross cell, the band-pass filter shows that the insertion loss is -1.9dB~ -1.6dB with a 3dB bandwidth of 8GHz, and the return loss is less than -8.9dB.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Array Electromagnetic Vibrator Combined Ultra Wide Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, high-power ultra wide band electromagnetic pulse source technology has developed rapidly. In order to better exert its value, there is an urgent need for a high-power ultra wide band antenna to effectively radiate electromagnetic energy. In this paper, the CST microwave studio is used to simulate the electromagnetic Vibrator Combined antenna to determine the size and shape of a single antenna. Then simulate the 3×3 array antenna. By changing the antenna spacing, it is found that: 1. The beam width in the horizontal plane is only related to the spacing of the antennas in the horizontal direction; 2. The beam width in the vertical plane is only related to the spacing of the antennas in the vertical direction; 3. The gain of the antenna fluctuates with the change of the antenna spacing, and remains basically stable at λ/4 ~ λ/2.

articleTitle: An 8-bit 80MS/s 2b/cycle SAR ADC for Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an 8-bit, 80MS/s Successive Approximation Register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) with 2bit/cycle structure for sensor application. By using two capacitor-DAC arrays, S-DAC and R-DAC, the proposed SAR ADC can obtain 2-bit in one comparison cycle. With split-capacitor structure and monotonic switching strategy, two DACs reduce the number of capacitors and save the ADC power consumption. The proposed asynchronous control logic speeds up the ADC. The proposed ADC achieves 46.17dB SNDR at 80MS/s rate with 1.8V supply voltage in 180nm CMOS process.

articleTitle: Effects of Druyvesteyn Distribution to Transmission Coefficients in Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The transmission coefficients for Druyvesteyn distribution function is the subject of this study. A Druyvesteyn distribution function is used to descrirbe the bounded plasma, and the complex permittivity for the plasma with Druyvesteyn distribution is derived. Based on this, the transmission of electromagnetic wave in the plasma with Druyvesteyn distribution and the Maxwellian distribution is also analyzed. The effects of collision frequency and electron density on the transmission are investigated. The results showed that there's a great deal of variability between Druyvesteyn distribution and Maxwellian distribution which is an idealized model to describe plasma. Comparing the results obtained, it is of great importance to analyze the interaction between electromagnetic waves and plasma and also provides a theoretical basis for the experiments.

articleTitle: EMR Field Distribution Analysis of Crystal Oscillator on PCB
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: On PCB (Printed Circuit Board), the crystal oscillator circuit is the main source of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) interference. The simulation and analysis of its EMR characteristics is one of the key tasks of PCB EMC (Electro Magnetic Compatibility) design. In this paper, the simulation models are established by HFSS, and the EMR characteristics of crystal oscillator in different cases are simulated and analyzed. And the relationships between the electric field intensity and frequency are got. The simulation result shows that the area of the larger field intensity is concentrated in the middle part of the two pipe feet. When the shell is grounded, the field intensity around the shell is almost 0. When the PCB wireway is connected, the field intensity changes to concentrate at the end of the wireway. When the grounding capacitance is connected, the maximum field intensity decreases by 77.02%. The conclusion of this research provides an important theoretical basis for improving the EMC design of PCB.

articleTitle: Design of 77GHz Differentially-Fed Antenna Array using Chebyshev Distribution
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presented a differentially-fed antenna array operating at 77 GHz. The series-fed antenna array is excited on the main radiation patch through coupled microstrip lines (MSLs), thus forming a mesh structure. In order to reduce the coupling effect, metallized vias are added between array columns. Then we change the feed form by adding two circulators. The antenna array has a bandwidth of about 3.5 GHz with respect to a return loss of 10dB. The 3 dB beam widths are 18 degrees and 30 degrees in the E-plane and the H-plane, respectively. The simulation result shows the good frequency stability of the gain at a certain bandwidth of the center frequency point.

articleTitle: Charge Storage Level Indicator for RF Energy Harvester based on Dual-ID Passive UHF RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Far-field RF energy harvesting is a convincing approach for energizing low-power wireless devices. In this work, we present a passive UHF RFID tag combined with an RF-energy harvester where a low-power switch circuitry changes the tag's ID as the voltage at the harvester's storage capacitor exceeds a certain threshold. This way, an RFID reader can receive the information on when the system is ready for running more advanced and energy-consuming functionalities. As a summary, our system switches the tag's ID as the voltage at the storage capacitor exceeds 0.7 V and our simulations predict that both tag IDs can be detected at the distance of more than 4.8 m while conforming to European UHF RFID emission regulations.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Extinction Coefficient of Dipoles Cloud
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the aim of fast calculation of the electromagnetic scattering of the large dipoles cloud (LDC), the LDC can be treated as the continuous medium. This paper presents a method to calculate the extinction coefficient of dipoles cloud with the Method of Moments (MOM). The influence of the sample volume on the calculation of the extinction coefficient is also analyzed in this work.

articleTitle: Comparasion of FDTD Analysis With Absorbing Boundary Condition Based on Inverted-F Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Planar inverted-F antenna analysed using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method with absorbing boundary condition (ABC) are demonstrated in this thesis. To compare the effective of absorbing boundary condition at absorbing evanescent wave, two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions algorithm of the FDTD method are presented, which are convention perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary conditions and convolutional Perfectly Matched Layer (CPML) absorbing boundary condition. Based upon the programming language of MATLAB, the FDTD method is realized. The antenna is simulated using Ansoft High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software, The simulation results agree fairly well with theoretical CPML analysis. The dimension of proposed antenna is ( 10.48×16×0.847) mm3 and its resonated at (2.23-5.89) GHz which cover the C-communication frequency band. Inverted-F antenna display omnidirectional radiation pattern and good peak gains across the operation bands.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Anti-jamming Algorithm of Antenna Array Based on Orthogonal Subspace Projection
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the adaptive anti-jamming algorithm of antenna array based on orthogonal subspace projection. Firstly, the mathematical foundation of subspace projection is discussed. Then the mathematical model of adaptive anti-jamming of antenna array is established, and the anti-interference algorithm of orthogonal subspace projection is derived. Finally, simulation software is used to simulate the anti-jamming effect of 6-array elements.

articleTitle: Ka band orthogonal dumbbell groove substrate integrated waveguide filter
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional microstrip filter and the metal waveguide filter are difficult to realize narrow band and integration at the same time in the Ka band, a Ka-band orthogonal dumbbell groove substrate integrated waveguide filter is proposed. The non-periodic slotted substrate integrated waveguide filter is fabricated by forming a vertical slotted structure by sequentially opening the longitudinal and lateral dumbbell grooves in the metal layer on the substrate integrated waveguide. The measured results show that the center frequency of the filter is 29.4 GHz, the bandwidth is 1.4 GHz, the maximum insertion loss is 2.5 dB, the in-band return loss is greater than 18 dB, the passband 1.5 GHz external suppression attenuation is greater than 20 dB, and the size is significantly reduced. The measured and simulated results are in good agreement, which shows it has high application value in engineering.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Grid DGTD Algorithm for Tetrahedral and Hexahedron Based on Virtual Element
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: DGTD (Time Domain Discontinuous Galerkin) is a new time domain algorithm with broad application prospects in recent years. When dividing the computational domain, the tetrahedral mesh can fit the fine structure of the object, but for objects with larger geometrical dimensions, gets mass unknown and takes up too much resources. If use hexahedral mesh, a step error is generated at the fine structure. Therefore, this paper proposes a swap boundary method for tetrahedral and hexahedron elements. Different sub-domains are divided by different grid elements, and virtual elements exchange numerical fluxes on the swap boundary. The feasibility of this method is verified by the radiation example of electric dipole.

articleTitle: Test Method for Target Full Spatial Polarization Characteristics by BRDF Test System
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to detect target full-space polarization characteristic by appropriate to backward detection and polarization imaging in short range in the target recognition, test method for full-space polarization characteristic, based on BRDF test system, was proposed. By BRDF test system, typical background samples were tested to get full-space scattering polarization characteristics. Targets were recognized by distinguishing typical background samples with target samples, through analyzing the scattered light intensity and full-space polarization characteristics. Test result proves that the test method by BRDF test system can effectively identify the targets in a typical environmental background.

articleTitle: Modulation-Specific Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Algorithm for Correlative Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Emitter localization via triangulation is a common task for spectrum management, and it is typically realized by angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation with correlative interferometers installed within fixed or mobile monitoring stations. The AoA estimation technique is addressed and a modulation-specific algorithm is proposed. Simulation results show that, for a specific set of modulation types, namely the ones which are noncircular, both the accuracy of AoA estimation and that of localization are improved.

articleTitle: A Novel Structure of FSS with Stable Property for Wireless Communication in S-band
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel FSS structure is proposed in this paper for wireless communication in S-band such as 2.4GHz, which is a multi-layer and compact structure combined with the conventional swastika and cross-shaped structure. The size of unit cell is 10mm*10mm, and the bandwidth is only 30MHz with superb characteristics of frequency filtering. The simulation results show that the frequency deviation does not exceed 10MHz, which means this structure has excellent angular stability. Moreover, with the alternate use of different substrates and the changing sizes of unit cell, the resonant frequency can be adjusted widely in S-band.

articleTitle: A High Gain CP Antenna with Extreme Radiation Aperture for Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high gain circularly polarized (CP) antenna with extreme radiation aperture in vehicle applications is proposed in the paper. The coverage of the radiation patch extended to the whole side of the dielectric substrate realizes the extreme radiation aperture, which can increase the utilization ratio of antenna aperture maximally. Besides, Taking advantage of the radiation from the side patch, and the application environment, the roof of the vehicle which is a great metal reflector beneath the antenna, wide beamwidth can be realized. A distinctive 90° phase difference feed network located beneath the ground plane and four symmetric feed probes via the dielectric substrate form the feed structure. Good circular polarization radiation performance and impedance matching are achieved by adjusting the design of the feed network and the position of the probes, that is the feed points. The antenna works at around 1.48 GHz to receive satellite signals, especially for vehicle satellite signal reception. Experimental results show that it has a high gain above 7 dB in the required range when put on the roof of the car. The overall size of the antenna is 0.247λ0×0.247λ0×0.247λ0 at 1.48 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Quasi-Yagi Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel quasi-Yagi antenna is presented based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs). In the new design, the antenna consists of a transition from a coplanar waveguide to an SSPPs waveguide, an SSPPs balun, an SSPPs driving dipole, and two SSPPs directors. The lengths of the driving dipole and director are approximately reduced by 32% and 27% compared with that of the conventional antenna in the free space without substrate, as a result of high phase constant on the SSPPs. Numerical simulations demonstrate good performance of the proposed structure, which has a gain of 8.7 dBi operating at 3 GHz. The proposed SSPPs quasi-Yagi antenna has potential value in wireless communication systems due to its compact dimension and good performance.

articleTitle: Research on Factors Affecting Sidelobe Level of Millimeter Wave Microstrip Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, 77GHz vehicle-borne anti-collision radar antenna is taken as an example to study and analyze the influence factors of millimeter-wave microstrip array antenna sidelobe level. The proposed antenna includes waveguide microstrip conversion, microstrip transmission line, and 10-element unequal amplitude microstrip array antenna. In order to reduce the sidelobe level (SLL), the surface current and the space electric field of the microstrip transmission line are analyzed. The SLL of the antenna is effectively reduced by changing the structure of the microstrip transmission line. When the conventional microstrip transmission line is used, the E-plane SLL of the antenna is -11.43dB. With the improved transmission line form, the SLL and gain are -19.41 dB and 14.43dB, with are increased by 8dB and 0.6dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of the Radome based on the Digital Beam Forming Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, the analysis model for the array antenna with radome is established, for optimal design on the radome based on the digital beam forming technique (DBF). The method was verified by simulated results. It was shown that, the performance of array antenna with radome can be greatly improved. The minimum BSE (Boresight Error) and other optimum performances of the antenna-radome system can be achieved.

articleTitle: Study on the Controlled Atmospheric Refractivity Fluctuation Impairing the Imaging Quality of the Heterodyne Detection Lidar
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the principle of heterodyne detection and the array-distributed atmospheric refractivity fluctuation by a coherent acoustic, the theoretical feasibility of coherent acoustic waves affecting lidar imaging by changing the additional phase is analyzed, and the theoretical model of changing the additional phase is established. According to the theoretical model, the echo phase of the imaging radar is simulated and the adopted acoustic array. A scaling experiment is designed to verify the engineering feasibility of the controlled atmospheric refractivity fluctuation impairing the imaging quality of the heterodyne detection lidar by coherent acoustic wave effects on transmission-coherent laser imaging path. The results of this paper have important theoretical significance for the development of new methods and technologies in the field of lidar interference.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Monostatic RCS by Calderón Multiplicative Preconditioner and Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As scattering problems of subwavelength are analyzed over a wide incident angle, the trouble from ill conditioned impedance matrix and repeated computation would be a challenge topic. A novel method is proposed by Calderón Multiplicative Preconditioner (CMP) combined with a incident source based on Compressive Sensing (CS) to solve this problem. With help of Generalized orthogonal matching pursuit (GOMP), monostatic RCS can be fast and accurate constructed with less measurements. Numerical simulation results have shown that the computational efficiency of monostatic RCS can be further improved.

articleTitle: A Signal Marker Method Based On Double Threshold Energy Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Cognitive radio energy detection algorithm is widely used in practical engineering, but its main shortcoming is that the judgment threshold is difficult, and it is difficult to set the threshold while taking into account both false alarm probability and leakage alarm probability, thus increasing the difficulty of signal marking in the spectrum. Therefore, on the basis of the traditional double-threshold energy detection, a signal marking method is proposed for the characteristic of the fluctuation of the average power of noise. The maximum holding method is used to further process the spectrum and mark the central frequency point. Then, on the basis of the double-threshold energy detection, the frequency points between the double-threshold are sampled and modeled, and the end points of the frequency band are marked, so as to achieve the purpose of signal marking.

articleTitle: Novel Microstrip Antenna Array with wideband Radar Cross Section Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel microstrip antenna array with reduced radar cross section (RCS) is presented in this paper by shaping the edges of the patch and using probe loading technology. The RCS of the proposed antenna array is significantly reduced between 4GHz and 13GHz under the condition that the incident wave is in grazing angle. The radiation characteristics of the proposed antenna array are well preserved compared with the reference antenna array, which implies the validity of this new RCS reduction method.

articleTitle: Simulation of the metamaterial structure based on curved surface
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-layer metamaterial structure based on two-dimensional (2D) curved surface substrate is simulated working in THz band. The simulated results showed some novel properties compared to the conventional planar metamaterial absorber. The metamaterial structure based on curved surface presented good reflectivity between 8 and 14 THz, with a FWHM bandwidth of 6THz. With the transmissivity zero, the incident plane wave is partly polarization converted and partly absorbed.

articleTitle: The Research Situation and Prospect on Artificial Ionospheric Modification of National University of Defense Technology HAO Research Group
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, our research group has actively explored the technology of artificial ionosphere modification and got some achievements.we carried out relevant researches in ionospheric heating by HF radio wave and ionospheric modification by releasing chemical substances, which has certain guiding significance for improving the utilization efficiency of ionosphere.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-band High Integrated Array Antenna with Wide Beam Width for Security Inspection
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband high integrated array antenna with wide beam width is proposed to realize the 3-dimensional imaging in the Ka-band active imaging system for security inspection. On the basis of the antenna element which is distinctively designed as a union of the open-ended waveguide and the microstrip feeding network, excellent radiating performance combined with compact structure would come true in comparison with traditional design scheme of the antenna element for security inspection. When aimed at high resolution and fast scanning speed, the array antenna adopts the high integrated arrangement scheme and takes full advantage of the polarization theory just as presented in this paper. Simulation results demonstrate that the array antenna possesses low VSWR of less than 1.5 and radiating gain of more than 6dB when the whole bandwidth of 26.5~31.5GHz is covered. And the cross polarization level of the receiving element and the axial ratio (AR) of the transmitting element can achieve as low as -20dB and 3dB respectively in the whole half-power beam width (HPBW) in excess of 60 degrees, which approves its practicality in imaging area for security inspection.

articleTitle: Genetic Optimization of General Regression Neural Network Applied to Feature Extraction of Brillouin Scattering Spectrum in BOTDA Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Distributed fiber sensing technology based on Brillouin optical time domain analysis (BOTDA) sensors is widely applied to monitoring the faults of civil engineering. There is a high requirement for the accuracy of Brillouin scattering spectrum feature extraction. Therefore, in order to extract the feature of Brillouin scattering spectrum in BOTDA sensors, a curve fitting method based on genetic algorithm (GA) optimized general regression neural network (GA-GRNN) is proposed in this paper. The stimulation data of different linewidth and signal-to-noise ratio(SNR) are analyzed by using the GA-GRNN algorithm, the results show that the GA-GRNN algorithm does well in extracting the feature of Brillouin scattering spectrum.

articleTitle: Case study of ion line spectra during modulated PMSE condition
publicationTitle: 2018 12th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on observations of EISCAT VHF radar, this study presents the analysis of ion line spectra within PMSE altitude (80-90 km) during heating experiment on 13 July 2007. The results show that the strength of ion lines during the heating moment is smaller as compared to its strength during unheated moments. In PMSE altitude no double humped spectra of ion line is observed during the heating moment, which is the general characteristic of ion line spectra above PMSE altitude. The intensity of ion line shows variations with altitude and time. During heating moment, the asymmetrical peaks of ion line can be discussed.
